81	# Commercial integration design (checkpoint 2A/2B)
82	
83	## Findings that shaped the design
84	
85	1. **The milestone model could not carry multi-instalment builds.** The database constrained collections to `deposit`, `final`, `first_retainer`, with commission rounded separately per milestone.
86	2. **Per-milestone rounding is exploitable across milestones.** Odd-penny payments split over several milestones each round up independently (e.g. 5p+10p+5p pays 7p where one cumulative rounding of 20p pays 6p). Historical `standard-v1` behaviour is left exactly as it was; the new model closes this for new plans.
87	3. **One plan version cannot cover several schedules.** Accepted plan versions are immutable and compared on acceptance, so a flexible schedule under `standard-v2` would have been rejected as "different terms". Each schedule therefore gets its own deterministic version (`standard-v2`, `standard-v2.deposit-completion`, `standard-v2.d150000`, `standard-v2.c<instalments>`, `bespoke-v1.<…>`).
88	4. **Ordinary registration's one-domain lead protection also blocks legitimate additional projects.** It is kept for ordinary registrations (partial unique index) and relaxed only for founder-approved additional claims.
89	
90	## Model
91	
92	- Milestones: `deposit`, `interim` (new, aggregates middle instalments), `final`, `first_retainer`. Migration 0073 widens the check constraint only; no data is rewritten.
93	- `commissionModel: "pooled-build-v1"`: commission on all build milestones is computed on one cumulative total (`commissionAt(groupTotal)`); the first retainer is its own group. Absent for historical plans, which keep per-milestone rounding.
94	- `commitment` snapshot stored inside the immutable contract terms: currency, build value, recurring fee, minimum term, minimum contract value, schedule id and instalments, approval and refund references. `parseCommissionTerms` validates it is internally consistent (schedule sums to build, contract value = build + fee × term, twelve months for `standard-v2`/`growth-only-v1`).
95	- Approval actor and timestamp come from the existing contract row (`created_by`, `accepted_at`) plus audit.
96	- **Terms are built server-side** (`buildAcceptedTerms`). Founders choose a plan, schedule and (for discounts) a reserved fee. Client-supplied pricing, rate and the server-only `approvedDiscountFeePence` are ignored or overwritten.
97	- Plans are **disabled by default** (`expansion_plan_settings`). Acceptance share-locks the setting row, so disabling and accepting serialise.
98	- Growth-only has no build milestones and records a £4,200 commitment; first £350 earns £105; further collections exceed the milestone cap and are rejected.
99	- Bespoke: founder-entered instalments; 30% unless a different rate is entered with an approval reference; first-retainer eligibility defaults to none.
100	- Refunds use the same pooled group, so a £200 partial refund on a £2,000 standard-v2 build calculates −£60 and, under the default `manual_review` treatment, is held without touching the ledger.
101	
102	## Not integrated yet
103	
104	Gating acceptance on market eligibility and unresolved exclusivity (2E), withdrawal allocation (2C), and achievement/referral counting (2D) have no implementation. The market and exclusivity gates the specification lists for contract acceptance are therefore **not enforced**.
105	# Partner operations: toolkit, meetings, governance gates (checkpoint 4)
106	
107	## Onboarding toolkit (manual fulfilment)
108	Fourteen catalogue items. Defaults are honest: features that exist in this software (referral identifier, joint-meeting requests) show *available*; everything external (dedicated email, CircleCard, brochures, Academy, prospects, personal webpage...) shows *planned*. A founder records status per partner; **evidence is mandatory before an item can be available or completed** (service and database). Only a published partner resource can be associated. Nothing is provisioned, bought or sent.
109	
110	## Meeting requests (manual)
111	Seven meeting types; one to five preferred times plus an IANA time zone; optional own opportunity. Lifecycle: requested, under review, information required, alternative proposed, confirmed, declined, cancelled, completed, with database-enforced transitions and a mandatory confirmed time. Partners submit, answer, accept an alternative and cancel; founders decide. Times are never invented, no calendar event is created and no invitation is sent. The tables have no link to commission, so founder attendance cannot reduce it.
112	
113	## Market eligibility and exclusivity (acceptance gates)
114	- **New** acceptance by any route, including legacy `standard-v1` terms, needs a founder-confirmed customer country in an approved market (`*` for legacy: any approved market; plan-based: the plan must be listed). **Existing accepted contracts are grandfathered**: they are never re-evaluated and collections, refunds and payouts on them continue under any later policy change.
115	- Exclusivity compares by founder-defined canonical sector where both sides are classified; a classified restriction can be cleared against an unclassified prospect only by a founder classification. Wording-only comparison remains the conservative fallback and always errs towards review. Exclusivity terms are immutable; corrections supersede.
116	- Decision point: `assertAcceptanceGates` inside the acceptance transaction, under the shared advisory lock 7102 (administration takes it exclusively).
117	
118	## Not built
119	Prospect research and allocation, partner-activation and applicant market gating, Founding Partner recognition, personal profiles.
120	# Discount allowances
121	
122	- **Default: none.** No policy row means no discount. Quantities are founder decisions (see FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md) and nothing is invented.
123	- Founder sets a per-partner policy: period, allowance count (0 to 50), permitted build fees (integer pence, below £2,000) and an approval reference. Periods cannot overlap; the count cannot be lowered below reserved or consumed use.
124	- Reservation is a founder action on an **approved** opportunity (scope approved, capacity reserved). It locks the policy row, checks the fee is permitted and the count unspent, and allows one active reservation per opportunity (unique partial index).
125	- Acceptance consumes the reservation in the same transaction as the contract; a fee that differs from the reservation, an expired period or a missing reservation is refused. Resolved reservations are immutable and undeletable (trigger).
126	- Free build (£0) uses the same path, still needs an enabled plan, approved scope, capacity, an accepted contract and a verified first retainer. Commission outcomes for £2,000 / £1,500 / £1,000 / £500 / £0 are £705 / £555 / £405 / £255 / £105 (unit and persisted-ledger tests).
127	- Partners see only their own remaining count. Partners cannot reserve, set policies or approve anything.
128	- Concurrency (real PostgreSQL, separate connections): two reservations against one slot admit one; six against three admit exactly three; a policy reduction racing a reservation never leaves use above the allowance.
129	# Market eligibility (checkpoint 3E, acceptance gate)
130	
131	- Table `expansion_markets`, **no rows by default**: every market, including the UK, is closed until a founder approves it. A database check refuses `approved` unless legal, accounting, privacy and operational review are recorded with an approval reference and at least one plan.
132	- The gate uses the **customer's** commercial market (`expansion_opportunities.customer_country`), not the partner's residence. A partner may propose it at registration, but it counts only once a **founder confirms it** (`customer_country_confirmed_by`, migration 0077). An unknown, unconfirmed country or an unapproved/suspended market, or a plan not listed for the market, blocks plan-based contract acceptance (HTTP 409).
133	- Currency stays GBP. No international pricing, tax or conversion exists.
134	- Suspension racing acceptance is serialised by a row share lock; tested on separate connections.
135	
136	## Enforcement points (checkpoint 5)
137	- **Applicant residence** (`partner_applications.residence_country`): recorded for information at review. It never authorises anything. International applicants can be reviewed and taken to onboarding.
138	- **Partner operating market** (`expansion_partners.operating_country`, default GB): must be an approved market before an invitation is issued and again, under advisory lock 7102, at the moment of activation. A refused activation consumes nothing. A founder can change it. If it later becomes unapproved, the partner's new progression stops while accepted contracts and the ledger are untouched.
139	- **Customer commercial market** (`expansion_opportunities.customer_country`): gates partner progression, founder scope approval, researched allocation and contract acceptance. Registration is a preliminary record and is not blocked.
140	- Everything fails closed on an unknown or unapproved market. The default operating market (GB) authorises nothing until it is approved with every review.
141	- Partner-facing refusals are one generic sentence; founders see specific reasons. Allocation also needs the receiving partner's operating market approved.
142	- Known limits (independent reviews, low severity): a partner-supplied customer country counts for progression **and for founder scope approval** before a founder confirms it, so capacity can be provisionally reserved first (acceptance still requires the confirmation); contract acceptance does not re-check the partner's operating market, so already scope-approved work and legitimate servicing continue; changing a partner's operating market takes no 7102 lock, so one in-flight partner request can pass a just-committed change.
143	- No international pricing, tax or currency conversion exists. Currency stays GBP.
144	# Customer sector exclusivity (checkpoint 3E, acceptance gate)
145	
146	- `expansion_exclusivities` records accepted contractual exclusivity (customer, sector, area, reference, dates). `expansion_exclusivity_decisions` is append-only founder decisions per (opportunity, exclusivity).
147	- Matching is deliberately conservative (`expansion-gates.ts`): an identical sector in an equal or nested area is **restricted**; a similar sector (shared word stem, e.g. dental/dentistry), an overlapping but non-nested area, an unknown or uncomparable sector or area (either side) is **review required**; only a positively different sector or area is clear; a customer is never restricted by its own exclusivity. Ampersands and "and" are treated alike.
148	- Restricted: only an **approved exception** releases it. Review required: a founder may record **cleared** or an exception. Decisions cannot be edited.
149	- Acceptance takes a shared advisory lock; creating, ending or deciding an exclusivity takes the exclusive lock, so a restriction committed first is always seen. Tested on separate connections.
150	- Partners see only a generic "commercial checks in progress" notice. Customer names, sectors, areas and agreement references stay founder-only (asserted in the service and browser tests).
151	
152	## Limits
153	
154	Matching is word-stem based, not semantic; it is not a legal determination and a synonym with no shared stem can still be cleared, so founders should record exclusivities in the vocabulary partners use. Dates use Europe/London and the expiry date is the first unprotected day. Exclusivity terms rows have no immutability trigger (only decisions do). If any exclusivity is active, any prospect with an unknown sector needs review. Exclusivity is checked at **acceptance** (plan path only), not yet at registration, allocation or scope review.
155	
156	## Geography (migration 0088): founder-approved area tree
157	Geography is decided from `expansion_areas` (a tree: North West England, Greater Manchester, Manchester) and `expansion_area_aliases` (another way an area is written), both founder-managed and append-only. For the same sector: a prospect whose area is **inside a protected area** (or contains it) is **restricted**; two areas that are both classified and neither contains the other are **positively different** and clear; **anything not in the taxonomy goes to a founder review and can never clear**. Wording and stop-word filtering no longer decide anything beyond identical or nested text. **Only a founder-entered area can clear**: a partner-typed opportunity location is an unverified assertion, so it can match (restricted) but a classified-disjoint result for it is downgraded to review (an independent review showed a partner could otherwise choose wording that clears a protected region). Disjointness clears only for researched candidates, whose areas founders enter. Founders must model sibling areas as non-overlapping (areas are append-only, so a modelling mistake cannot be edited; define carefully), and must define the areas they want matched; with an empty taxonomy every non-identical area comparison for a same-sector exclusivity is a review (safe, but noisy). Examples proven in tests: North West England / Manchester, Nottinghamshire / Hucknall, Greater London / Westminster.
158	
159	## Checkpoint 5: where the check now applies
160	Registration (a preliminary record), founder scope approval, researched-candidate eligibility and allocation, and contract acceptance. **Partner requests are never evaluated against exclusivity**: an independent review showed that any difference in outcome, even with identical wording, lets a partner probe which sectors and areas are protected, one bit per attempt. Partner progression is therefore gated on markets only (markets are not confidential), and founders enforce exclusivity where a partner cannot observe the result. Candidate-level clearance is allowed only for a review-level match and is copied onto the opportunity at allocation; a confirmed restriction can only be released by an approved exception on an opportunity.
161	# Commission rules
162	
163	All authoritative amounts are integer pence. Versioned contract terms are snapshotted at approval and immutable after acceptance. Standard illustrative rates are 3000 basis points on website revenue and the first Growth Partnership payment: 100000 -> 30000; 100000 -> 30000; 35000 -> 10500; total 70500. Later retainers have no entitlement in the initial plan.
164	
165	Only authorised manual verification of qualifying VAT-exclusive collected revenue can earn commission. Each collection has an immutable external reference, invoice link, verifier and evidence reference. Partial payments use cumulative rounding so splitting payments cannot increase entitlement. Over-collection, duplicate references with different content, invalid states and over-refunds must fail closed. Identical event replay returns the original result without a second ledger entry.
166	
167	Custom pricing/rates require explicit founder approval; no partner can edit accepted contract terms or create financial events. Pending contractual maximum is conditional, never earned. Refunds append approved reversals with reasons under the final reviewed agreement; no automatic recovery. Payout preparation locks eligible ledger entries, binds an invoice/reference, requires manual approval and records reconciliation. Nothing in this implementation authorises transfers or self-billing.
168	
169	Business/legal decisions still required: partner VAT treatment, applicable refund entitlement, invoice requirements, dispute resolution, lead protection term, applicant retention and agreement language. These are release prerequisites, not automated legal conclusions.
170	# Commercial activation gates
171	
172	| Mode | Runtime settings and approvals |
173	| --- | --- |
174	| Local demonstration | Use a disposable local database and synthetic records. Explicitly opt in to local intake or activation as necessary for a test. Keep integrations and real transfer activity off. |
175	| Deployed but closed | Separately approve deployment and informational page publication. Set `PARTNER_APPLICATIONS_ENABLED=false`, `PARTNER_ACTIVATION_ENABLED=false` and `PARTNER_RETENTION_EXECUTION_ENABLED=false`. |
176	| Recruitment open | Approve the public notice, period, data handling and review owner. Set the valid privacy version and retention days, then explicitly enable intake. Keep activation closed. |
177	| Controlled commercial pilot | Resolve partner terms, privacy, accounting, lead protection, resources, marketing and delivery gates. Approve the exact pilot scope before enabling invitation issuance and activation. Record the individual founder confirmations and agreement version for each partner. |
178	
179	Invitation issuance and token consumption both require the admin activation switch. Existing authenticated partners are managed through individual revocation. Turning the new-activation switch off does not revoke those accounts. Keep a dated release decision reference for the mode transition. The existing onboarding confirmations record agreement, legal review, independent status and operational review independently, with a founder and timestamp for each saved review. Record the source agreement, commercial decisions, account setup checks and individual acceptance evidence in the controlled onboarding record. Configuration and founder confirmation fields cannot verify an adviser's decision by themselves.
180	
181	## Founder decisions
182	
183	Rhys and Trev can record the decision, date, owner, approved option and source reference against each row. The listed owners are proposed for review.
184	
185	| Decision | Owner or adviser | Options and risk to resolve | Blocks |
186	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
187	| Independent status and agreement | Founders, employment solicitor | Assess the working arrangement. Agree obligations, boundaries, acceptance evidence and versioning. Incorrect classification or an unrecorded agreement creates exposure. | Activation |
188	| Commission entitlement | Trev, solicitor and accountant | Approve collection basis, eligible milestones and exceptions. Use explicit prospective versions for bespoke terms. Ambiguity leads to disputes. | Activation, finance |
189	| Lead protection and attribution disputes | Trev and Rhys | Set start, expiry, reassignment, canonical customer priority, evidence and dispute owner. An indefinite claim can stall opportunities. | Activation |
190	| Refund eligibility and previously paid adjustments | Trev, solicitor and accountant | Require agreement-backed review. Determine when a refund changes entitlement and whether already-paid commission can be netted, disputed or pursued. Preserve history. | Finance |
191	| Clawback, settlement and external recovery | Trev and solicitor | Default to no automated recovery. Decide any exceptional manual process, evidence and approval authority. | Finance |
192	| Partner invoices and VAT | Accountant and Trev | Define invoice checks, tax treatment, VAT-inclusive payment and evidence handling for registered and unregistered partners. Require separate approval for any self-billing. | Finance |
193	| Payout frequency and authority | Trev and accountant | Choose a manual cycle, invoice cut-off, reconciliation evidence and standing approval ownership. Incomplete checks create double-payment risk. | Finance |
194	| Applicant notice, lawful basis and retention | Rhys and privacy adviser | Approve fields, versions, category durations, holds, rights contact and erasure after restore. A missing decision delays intake. | Recruitment, activation |
195	| Marketing process | Trev and privacy adviser | Approve permitted channels, acquisition source, screening evidence, opt-out handling and training. Keep unsolicited outreach on hold until the process is approved. | Activation |
196	| Approved resources | Trev and Rhys | Review claims, partner-only and client-facing classifications, expiry and publication owner. | Activation |
197	| Initial capacity and partner limit | Trev and delivery owner | Set an assessed delivery allocation and explicit cohort cap. Review before commitments and expansion. | Activation |
198	| Operational ownership | Both founders | Name recruitment, privacy, finance, monitoring, delivery, incident and recovery owners and deputies. | Recruitment, activation, finance |
199	| Deployment approval | Named release approver | Approve exact reviewed SHA, check results, backup and rollout windows. | Deployment |
200	| Public recruitment launch | Both founders | Decide between closed informational publication and controlled intake after review staffing and privacy sign-off. | Recruitment |
201	
202	## Marketing and suppression
203	
204	Canonical duplicate and suppression checks are registration controls. Treat each prospect as **not assessed for outreach** until an authorised person checks the evidence for the proposed channel. Record provenance, date, operator, subscriber type and objection outcome in the approved private process. For live UK B2B marketing calls, the ICO directs organisations to check TPS, CTPS and their own do-not-call lists, subject to applicable permissions and exceptions. Electronic marketing rules vary by subscriber type and channel. Make objections and opt-outs available to partners without exposing unrelated prospect data. [ICO business-to-business marketing guidance](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/)
205	
206	No live TPS/CTPS integration or completed screening is established by this change. Determine the approved screening account and access process, the source of objection updates and a named person responsible for prompt suppression. Use an approved correction process when a partner disputes a duplicate or suppression.

# Commercial integration design (checkpoint 2A/2B)

## Findings that shaped the design

1. **The milestone model could not carry multi-instalment builds.** The database constrained collections to `deposit`, `final`, `first_retainer`, with commission rounded separately per milestone.
2. **Per-milestone rounding is exploitable across milestones.** Odd-penny payments split over several milestones each round up independently (e.g. 5p+10p+5p pays 7p where one cumulative rounding of 20p pays 6p). Historical `standard-v1` behaviour is left exactly as it was; the new model closes this for new plans.
3. **One plan version cannot cover several schedules.** Accepted plan versions are immutable and compared on acceptance, so a flexible schedule under `standard-v2` would have been rejected as "different terms". Each schedule therefore gets its own deterministic version (`standard-v2`, `standard-v2.deposit-completion`, `standard-v2.d150000`, `standard-v2.c<instalments>`, `bespoke-v1.<…>`).
4. **Ordinary registration's one-domain lead protection also blocks legitimate additional projects.** It is kept for ordinary registrations (partial unique index) and relaxed only for founder-approved additional claims.

## Model

- Milestones: `deposit`, `interim` (new, aggregates middle instalments), `final`, `first_retainer`. Migration 0073 widens the check constraint only; no data is rewritten.
- `commissionModel: "pooled-build-v1"`: commission on all build milestones is computed on one cumulative total (`commissionAt(groupTotal)`); the first retainer is its own group. Absent for historical plans, which keep per-milestone rounding.
- `commitment` snapshot stored inside the immutable contract terms: currency, build value, recurring fee, minimum term, minimum contract value, schedule id and instalments, approval and refund references. `parseCommissionTerms` validates it is internally consistent (schedule sums to build, contract value = build + fee × term, twelve months for `standard-v2`/`growth-only-v1`).
- Approval actor and timestamp come from the existing contract row (`created_by`, `accepted_at`) plus audit.
- **Terms are built server-side** (`buildAcceptedTerms`). Founders choose a plan, schedule and (for discounts) a reserved fee. Client-supplied pricing, rate and the server-only `approvedDiscountFeePence` are ignored or overwritten.
- Plans are **disabled by default** (`expansion_plan_settings`). Acceptance share-locks the setting row, so disabling and accepting serialise.
- Growth-only has no build milestones and records a £4,200 commitment; first £350 earns £105; further collections exceed the milestone cap and are rejected.
- Bespoke: founder-entered instalments; 30% unless a different rate is entered with an approval reference; first-retainer eligibility defaults to none.
- Refunds use the same pooled group, so a £200 partial refund on a £2,000 standard-v2 build calculates −£60 and, under the default `manual_review` treatment, is held without touching the ledger.

## Not integrated yet

Gating acceptance on market eligibility and unresolved exclusivity (2E), withdrawal allocation (2C), and achievement/referral counting (2D) have no implementation. The market and exclusivity gates the specification lists for contract acceptance are therefore **not enforced**.
# Partner operations: toolkit, meetings, governance gates (checkpoint 4)

## Onboarding toolkit (manual fulfilment)
Fourteen catalogue items. Defaults are honest: features that exist in this software (referral identifier, joint-meeting requests) show *available*; everything external (dedicated email, CircleCard, brochures, Academy, prospects, personal webpage...) shows *planned*. A founder records status per partner; **evidence is mandatory before an item can be available or completed** (service and database). Only a published partner resource can be associated. Nothing is provisioned, bought or sent.

## Meeting requests (manual)
Seven meeting types; one to five preferred times plus an IANA time zone; optional own opportunity. Lifecycle: requested, under review, information required, alternative proposed, confirmed, declined, cancelled, completed, with database-enforced transitions and a mandatory confirmed time. Partners submit, answer, accept an alternative and cancel; founders decide. Times are never invented, no calendar event is created and no invitation is sent. The tables have no link to commission, so founder attendance cannot reduce it.

## Market eligibility and exclusivity (acceptance gates)
- **New** acceptance by any route, including legacy `standard-v1` terms, needs a founder-confirmed customer country in an approved market (`*` for legacy: any approved market; plan-based: the plan must be listed). **Existing accepted contracts are grandfathered**: they are never re-evaluated and collections, refunds and payouts on them continue under any later policy change.
- Exclusivity compares by founder-defined canonical sector where both sides are classified; a classified restriction can be cleared against an unclassified prospect only by a founder classification. Wording-only comparison remains the conservative fallback and always errs towards review. Exclusivity terms are immutable; corrections supersede.
- Decision point: `assertAcceptanceGates` inside the acceptance transaction, under the shared advisory lock 7102 (administration takes it exclusively).

## Not built
Prospect research and allocation, partner-activation and applicant market gating, Founding Partner recognition, personal profiles.
# Discount allowances

- **Default: none.** No policy row means no discount. Quantities are founder decisions (see FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md) and nothing is invented.
- Founder sets a per-partner policy: period, allowance count (0 to 50), permitted build fees (integer pence, below £2,000) and an approval reference. Periods cannot overlap; the count cannot be lowered below reserved or consumed use.
- Reservation is a founder action on an **approved** opportunity (scope approved, capacity reserved). It locks the policy row, checks the fee is permitted and the count unspent, and allows one active reservation per opportunity (unique partial index).
- Acceptance consumes the reservation in the same transaction as the contract; a fee that differs from the reservation, an expired period or a missing reservation is refused. Resolved reservations are immutable and undeletable (trigger).
- Free build (£0) uses the same path, still needs an enabled plan, approved scope, capacity, an accepted contract and a verified first retainer. Commission outcomes for £2,000 / £1,500 / £1,000 / £500 / £0 are £705 / £555 / £405 / £255 / £105 (unit and persisted-ledger tests).
- Partners see only their own remaining count. Partners cannot reserve, set policies or approve anything.
- Concurrency (real PostgreSQL, separate connections): two reservations against one slot admit one; six against three admit exactly three; a policy reduction racing a reservation never leaves use above the allowance.
# Market eligibility (checkpoint 3E, acceptance gate)

- Table `expansion_markets`, **no rows by default**: every market, including the UK, is closed until a founder approves it. A database check refuses `approved` unless legal, accounting, privacy and operational review are recorded with an approval reference and at least one plan.
- The gate uses the **customer's** commercial market (`expansion_opportunities.customer_country`), not the partner's residence. A partner may propose it at registration, but it counts only once a **founder confirms it** (`customer_country_confirmed_by`, migration 0077). An unknown, unconfirmed country or an unapproved/suspended market, or a plan not listed for the market, blocks plan-based contract acceptance (HTTP 409).
- Currency stays GBP. No international pricing, tax or conversion exists.
- Suspension racing acceptance is serialised by a row share lock; tested on separate connections.

## Enforcement points (checkpoint 5)
- **Applicant residence** (`partner_applications.residence_country`): recorded for information at review. It never authorises anything. International applicants can be reviewed and taken to onboarding.
- **Partner operating market** (`expansion_partners.operating_country`, default GB): must be an approved market before an invitation is issued and again, under advisory lock 7102, at the moment of activation. A refused activation consumes nothing. A founder can change it. If it later becomes unapproved, the partner's new progression stops while accepted contracts and the ledger are untouched.
- **Customer commercial market** (`expansion_opportunities.customer_country`): gates partner progression, founder scope approval, researched allocation and contract acceptance. Registration is a preliminary record and is not blocked.
- Everything fails closed on an unknown or unapproved market. The default operating market (GB) authorises nothing until it is approved with every review.
- Partner-facing refusals are one generic sentence; founders see specific reasons. Allocation also needs the receiving partner's operating market approved.
- Known limits (independent reviews, low severity): a partner-supplied customer country counts for progression **and for founder scope approval** before a founder confirms it, so capacity can be provisionally reserved first (acceptance still requires the confirmation); contract acceptance does not re-check the partner's operating market, so already scope-approved work and legitimate servicing continue; changing a partner's operating market takes no 7102 lock, so one in-flight partner request can pass a just-committed change.
- No international pricing, tax or currency conversion exists. Currency stays GBP.
# Customer sector exclusivity (checkpoint 3E, acceptance gate)

- `expansion_exclusivities` records accepted contractual exclusivity (customer, sector, area, reference, dates). `expansion_exclusivity_decisions` is append-only founder decisions per (opportunity, exclusivity).
- Matching is deliberately conservative (`expansion-gates.ts`): an identical sector in an equal or nested area is **restricted**; a similar sector (shared word stem, e.g. dental/dentistry), an overlapping but non-nested area, an unknown or uncomparable sector or area (either side) is **review required**; only a positively different sector or area is clear; a customer is never restricted by its own exclusivity. Ampersands and "and" are treated alike.
- Restricted: only an **approved exception** releases it. Review required: a founder may record **cleared** or an exception. Decisions cannot be edited.
- Acceptance takes a shared advisory lock; creating, ending or deciding an exclusivity takes the exclusive lock, so a restriction committed first is always seen. Tested on separate connections.
- Partners see only a generic "commercial checks in progress" notice. Customer names, sectors, areas and agreement references stay founder-only (asserted in the service and browser tests).

## Limits

Matching is word-stem based, not semantic; it is not a legal determination and a synonym with no shared stem can still be cleared, so founders should record exclusivities in the vocabulary partners use. Dates use Europe/London and the expiry date is the first unprotected day. Exclusivity terms rows have no immutability trigger (only decisions do). If any exclusivity is active, any prospect with an unknown sector needs review. Exclusivity is checked at **acceptance** (plan path only), not yet at registration, allocation or scope review.

## Geography (migration 0088): founder-approved area tree
Geography is decided from `expansion_areas` (a tree: North West England, Greater Manchester, Manchester) and `expansion_area_aliases` (another way an area is written), both founder-managed and append-only. For the same sector: a prospect whose area is **inside a protected area** (or contains it) is **restricted**; two areas that are both classified and neither contains the other are **positively different** and clear; **anything not in the taxonomy goes to a founder review and can never clear**. Wording and stop-word filtering no longer decide anything beyond identical or nested text. **Only a founder-entered area can clear**: a partner-typed opportunity location is an unverified assertion, so it can match (restricted) but a classified-disjoint result for it is downgraded to review (an independent review showed a partner could otherwise choose wording that clears a protected region). Disjointness clears only for researched candidates, whose areas founders enter. Founders must model sibling areas as non-overlapping (areas are append-only, so a modelling mistake cannot be edited; define carefully), and must define the areas they want matched; with an empty taxonomy every non-identical area comparison for a same-sector exclusivity is a review (safe, but noisy). Examples proven in tests: North West England / Manchester, Nottinghamshire / Hucknall, Greater London / Westminster.

## Checkpoint 5: where the check now applies
Registration (a preliminary record), founder scope approval, researched-candidate eligibility and allocation, and contract acceptance. **Partner requests are never evaluated against exclusivity**: an independent review showed that any difference in outcome, even with identical wording, lets a partner probe which sectors and areas are protected, one bit per attempt. Partner progression is therefore gated on markets only (markets are not confidential), and founders enforce exclusivity where a partner cannot observe the result. Candidate-level clearance is allowed only for a review-level match and is copied onto the opportunity at allocation; a confirmed restriction can only be released by an approved exception on an opportunity.
# Commission rules

All authoritative amounts are integer pence. Versioned contract terms are snapshotted at approval and immutable after acceptance. Standard illustrative rates are 3000 basis points on website revenue and the first Growth Partnership payment: 100000 -> 30000; 100000 -> 30000; 35000 -> 10500; total 70500. Later retainers have no entitlement in the initial plan.

Only authorised manual verification of qualifying VAT-exclusive collected revenue can earn commission. Each collection has an immutable external reference, invoice link, verifier and evidence reference. Partial payments use cumulative rounding so splitting payments cannot increase entitlement. Over-collection, duplicate references with different content, invalid states and over-refunds must fail closed. Identical event replay returns the original result without a second ledger entry.

Custom pricing/rates require explicit founder approval; no partner can edit accepted contract terms or create financial events. Pending contractual maximum is conditional, never earned. Refunds append approved reversals with reasons under the final reviewed agreement; no automatic recovery. Payout preparation locks eligible ledger entries, binds an invoice/reference, requires manual approval and records reconciliation. Nothing in this implementation authorises transfers or self-billing.

Business/legal decisions still required: partner VAT treatment, applicable refund entitlement, invoice requirements, dispute resolution, lead protection term, applicant retention and agreement language. These are release prerequisites, not automated legal conclusions.
# Commercial activation gates

| Mode | Runtime settings and approvals |
| --- | --- |
| Local demonstration | Use a disposable local database and synthetic records. Explicitly opt in to local intake or activation as necessary for a test. Keep integrations and real transfer activity off. |
| Deployed but closed | Separately approve deployment and informational page publication. Set `PARTNER_APPLICATIONS_ENABLED=false`, `PARTNER_ACTIVATION_ENABLED=false` and `PARTNER_RETENTION_EXECUTION_ENABLED=false`. |
| Recruitment open | Approve the public notice, period, data handling and review owner. Set the valid privacy version and retention days, then explicitly enable intake. Keep activation closed. |
| Controlled commercial pilot | Resolve partner terms, privacy, accounting, lead protection, resources, marketing and delivery gates. Approve the exact pilot scope before enabling invitation issuance and activation. Record the individual founder confirmations and agreement version for each partner. |

Invitation issuance and token consumption both require the admin activation switch. Existing authenticated partners are managed through individual revocation. Turning the new-activation switch off does not revoke those accounts. Keep a dated release decision reference for the mode transition. The existing onboarding confirmations record agreement, legal review, independent status and operational review independently, with a founder and timestamp for each saved review. Record the source agreement, commercial decisions, account setup checks and individual acceptance evidence in the controlled onboarding record. Configuration and founder confirmation fields cannot verify an adviser's decision by themselves.

## Founder decisions

Rhys and Trev can record the decision, date, owner, approved option and source reference against each row. The listed owners are proposed for review.

| Decision | Owner or adviser | Options and risk to resolve | Blocks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Independent status and agreement | Founders, employment solicitor | Assess the working arrangement. Agree obligations, boundaries, acceptance evidence and versioning. Incorrect classification or an unrecorded agreement creates exposure. | Activation |
| Commission entitlement | Trev, solicitor and accountant | Approve collection basis, eligible milestones and exceptions. Use explicit prospective versions for bespoke terms. Ambiguity leads to disputes. | Activation, finance |
| Lead protection and attribution disputes | Trev and Rhys | Set start, expiry, reassignment, canonical customer priority, evidence and dispute owner. An indefinite claim can stall opportunities. | Activation |
| Refund eligibility and previously paid adjustments | Trev, solicitor and accountant | Require agreement-backed review. Determine when a refund changes entitlement and whether already-paid commission can be netted, disputed or pursued. Preserve history. | Finance |
| Clawback, settlement and external recovery | Trev and solicitor | Default to no automated recovery. Decide any exceptional manual process, evidence and approval authority. | Finance |
| Partner invoices and VAT | Accountant and Trev | Define invoice checks, tax treatment, VAT-inclusive payment and evidence handling for registered and unregistered partners. Require separate approval for any self-billing. | Finance |
| Payout frequency and authority | Trev and accountant | Choose a manual cycle, invoice cut-off, reconciliation evidence and standing approval ownership. Incomplete checks create double-payment risk. | Finance |
| Applicant notice, lawful basis and retention | Rhys and privacy adviser | Approve fields, versions, category durations, holds, rights contact and erasure after restore. A missing decision delays intake. | Recruitment, activation |
| Marketing process | Trev and privacy adviser | Approve permitted channels, acquisition source, screening evidence, opt-out handling and training. Keep unsolicited outreach on hold until the process is approved. | Activation |
| Approved resources | Trev and Rhys | Review claims, partner-only and client-facing classifications, expiry and publication owner. | Activation |
| Initial capacity and partner limit | Trev and delivery owner | Set an assessed delivery allocation and explicit cohort cap. Review before commitments and expansion. | Activation |
| Operational ownership | Both founders | Name recruitment, privacy, finance, monitoring, delivery, incident and recovery owners and deputies. | Recruitment, activation, finance |
| Deployment approval | Named release approver | Approve exact reviewed SHA, check results, backup and rollout windows. | Deployment |
| Public recruitment launch | Both founders | Decide between closed informational publication and controlled intake after review staffing and privacy sign-off. | Recruitment |

## Marketing and suppression

Canonical duplicate and suppression checks are registration controls. Treat each prospect as **not assessed for outreach** until an authorised person checks the evidence for the proposed channel. Record provenance, date, operator, subscriber type and objection outcome in the approved private process. For live UK B2B marketing calls, the ICO directs organisations to check TPS, CTPS and their own do-not-call lists, subject to applicable permissions and exceptions. Electronic marketing rules vary by subscriber type and channel. Make objections and opt-outs available to partners without exposing unrelated prospect data. [ICO business-to-business marketing guidance](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/)

No live TPS/CTPS integration or completed screening is established by this change. Determine the approved screening account and access process, the source of objection updates and a named person responsible for prompt suppression. Use an approved correction process when a partner disputes a duplicate or suppression.

/**
 * Founder-published starting prices for the public site.
 *
 * A starting price is the entry point for an agreed scope. It is not unlimited
 * design, development, marketing, support, integrations or a guaranteed outcome.
 * Prices are GBP only. Do not publish fixed conversions into other currencies.
 *
 * These figures are intentionally not wired through the public-claims registry.
 * Older draft rate-card rows still exist in migration history and must not
 * override this published guidance until the founders verify a replacement.
 */

export const STARTING_PRICE_BOUNDARY =
  "A starting price is the entry point for an agreed scope. It is not unlimited development, marketing, support, integrations or a guaranteed result. Every proposal depends on requirements, complexity and the deliverables we write down. Prices are in GBP. We do not bill in other currencies or publish fixed converted prices."

export interface PublishedStartingPrice {
  id: "website" | "partnership" | "audit" | "email"
  name: string
  priceLabel: string
  /** Minimum published amount in major GBP units. Null when the figure is a fixed fee rather than a minimum. */
  minPrice: number | null
  /** Fixed published fee, when the offer is not a "from" price. */
  price: number | null
  unitText: string
  note: string
  href: string
  cta: string
}

export const publishedStartingPrices: readonly PublishedStartingPrice[] = [
  {
    id: "website",
    name: "Website design and development",
    priceLabel: "From £2,000",
    minPrice: 2000,
    price: null,
    unitText: "project",
    note: "A starting point for an agreed website project. Content, pages, integrations, migration and support are set in the proposal.",
    href: "/quote",
    cta: "Get a Website Quote",
  },
  {
    id: "partnership",
    name: "Growth Partnership",
    priceLabel: "From £350/month",
    minPrice: 350,
    price: null,
    unitText: "month",
    note: "An entry point for an agreed service scope. It is not an unlimited marketing package. Priorities and cadence are written down before work starts.",
    href: "/digital-growth-partnership",
    cta: "Explore Growth Partnerships",
  },
  {
    id: "audit",
    name: "Business Growth Audit",
    priceLabel: "£395",
    minPrice: null,
    price: 395,
    unitText: "audit",
    note: "A one-time review and prioritised roadmap. Where the published terms apply, the full fee is credited against an eligible subsequent ScaleSmiths build.",
    href: "/services/business-growth-audit",
    cta: "Request a Business Audit",
  },
  {
    id: "email",
    name: "Business email",
    priceLabel: "From £15/month",
    minPrice: 15,
    price: null,
    unitText: "month",
    note: "Three professional 5GB mailboxes on your domain, with initial setup included. Extra mailboxes are not included unless agreed.",
    href: "/services/managed-business-email",
    cta: "Set up business email",
  },
]

/** Budget choices on the public project brief. These follow the published starting prices. */
export const publicProjectBudgetOptions = [
  "Website from £2,000",
  "Growth Partnership from £350/month",
  "Larger build, scoped after discovery",
  "Not sure yet",
] as const

export function publishedStartingPrice(id: PublishedStartingPrice["id"]) {
  const match = publishedStartingPrices.find((item) => item.id === id)
  if (!match) throw new Error(`Unknown published starting price: ${id}`)
  return match
}

export function buildPublishedOfferCatalog(baseUrl = "https://scalesmiths.co.uk") {
  const base = baseUrl.replace(/\/$/, "")
  return {
    "@context": "https://schema.org",
    "@type": "OfferCatalog",
    name: "ScaleSmiths published starting prices",
    url: `${base}/pricing#published-prices`,
    itemListElement: publishedStartingPrices.map((item) => ({
      "@type": "Offer",
      name: item.name,
      url: `${base}${item.href}`,
      priceCurrency: "GBP",
      description: `${item.note} ${STARTING_PRICE_BOUNDARY}`,
      ...(item.price != null
        ? { price: item.price }
        : {
            priceSpecification: {
              "@type": "PriceSpecification",
              minPrice: item.minPrice,
              priceCurrency: "GBP",
              unitText: item.unitText,
            },
          }),
    })),
  }
}
/**
 * Commercial engagement models shown on the homepage and pricing journeys.
 * Starting prices stay published on /pricing; they are not the homepage lead narrative.
 */
export const engagementModels = [
  {
    id: "business-websites-growth",
    eyebrow: "Transparent entry points",
    title: "Business Websites & Growth",
    description:
      "Practical websites, audits, managed email and Growth Partnerships for ambitious independent and growing businesses. Starting prices stay published; scope is agreed before work begins.",
    href: "/pricing#web-growth",
    cta: "View starting prices",
    secondaryHref: "/digital-growth-partnership",
    secondaryCta: "Growth Partnership",
  },
  {
    id: "established-transformation",
    eyebrow: "Corporate digital estate",
    title: "Established Business Transformation",
    description:
      "Evolution of websites, customer journeys, integrations and operational efficiency for multi-site and established organisations that have outgrown a brochure presence.",
    href: "/enterprise-websites",
    cta: "Enterprise websites",
    secondaryHref: "/enterprise",
    secondaryCta: "Enterprise systems",
  },
  {
    id: "custom-platforms-enterprise",
    eyebrow: "Independently scoped",
    title: "Custom Platforms & Enterprise Projects",
    description:
      "Bespoke architecture, workflows, security, migrations and support for complex platforms. Never sold against a website starting price. Scoped after discovery.",
    href: "/pricing#enterprise-systems",
    cta: "How complex work is priced",
    secondaryHref: "/custom-systems",
    secondaryCta: "Custom systems",
  },
] as const

export type EngagementModel = (typeof engagementModels)[number]

63 "Yes. We start by reviewing what the current site already does well === pages that rank, enquiries it generates, integrations and hosting === and then recommend a rebuild, a focused repair or a migration, whichever the evidence supports.",
69 "Yes. Published work runs on self-hosted Docker Compose and Nginx setups on a VPS as well as managed platforms such as Vercel, chosen around the workload and the support model rather than sold as an anonymous storage allowance. Hosting can be arranged as part of a build or as a managed service on its own.",
75 "Often, after a technical review of the current code, licence terms, data, deployment process and connected services. Pinkys Prints is a published example: a Shopify store rebuilt as a custom platform and moved from managed cloud services onto self-hosted infrastructure. We map existing URLs, metadata and internal links before a migration to reduce avoidable search disruption.",
81 "Discovery covers what you sell, who buys it, how they currently choose you, what the present site or system does well, and what evidence exists, analytics, Search Console, enquiry records. Practically, projects move fastest when content, imagery, brand assets and access to domains, hosting and any integrated systems are identified early, because content readiness affects the schedule more than page count does.",
87 "Yes. Pinkys Prints is a custom e-commerce platform with catalogue variants and a tailored product admin, migrated from Shopify. We recommend custom commerce only when the operational value justifies owning it; where an established platform already fits, configuring and integrating it is usually the better decision.",
94 "Search engine optimisation is the work that makes a website findable, understandable and worth choosing in search results. In practice it splits into three parts: the technical foundations that let search engines crawl and index pages, the content that answers what people are actually searching for, and the on-page experience that turns a click into an enquiry. It is ongoing work, not a one-off setting.",
100 "Local SEO is search work aimed at people looking for a provider in a particular place, searches with an area in them, and searches where results are shaped by where the person is. It covers how clearly the site describes each service and the areas covered, how consistent the business details are across the web, how the Google Business Profile supports the site, and whether the proof a local buyer needs is actually visible.",
106 "Longer than most sales pitches suggest, and it varies with the starting point. Technical fixes can change indexation quickly; content and authority work is measured over months, not weeks. Anyone quoting a fixed timescale before looking at your current visibility, competition and site health is guessing.",
112 "No. Rankings depend on Google's systems, your competitors and the searcher, none of which any agency controls. We will not promise a position. What can be committed to is the work itself: technical health, content that matches real search intent, credible proof, and measurement against a recorded baseline so progress is judged on evidence.",
118 "Search foundations are part of the build: deliberate metadata, canonicals, structured data, heading and route architecture, internal links, indexation controls and page speed. Ongoing SEO === content, authority, continued measurement and iteration === is separate work, scoped either as a project or through a Growth Partnership.",
124 "Technical SEO is everything that determines whether a search engine can reach, render, understand and trust your pages: crawlability and robots rules, canonical URLs, sitemaps, redirects, structured data, heading hierarchy, mobile rendering, Core Web Vitals and HTTPS. It rarely wins attention on its own, but content cannot perform if the technical layer is working against it.",
130 "They solve different problems. Ads buy visibility immediately and stop when the budget does; SEO compounds slowly and keeps working. Which mix is right depends on how urgently you need enquiries, your margin per customer and how competitive the terms are. We will say plainly when paid search is the more honest answer for a given timeframe.",
136 "Yes, and that is often the better starting point. An SEO and website audit reviews indexation, technical health, content coverage, internal linking and the conversion journey, and produces a prioritised list. Implementation can then be scoped separately, handled through a Growth Partnership, or carried out by your own team.",
142 "The usual causes, in the order we find them: the pages are not indexed at all (blocked by robots rules, a noindex tag or a staging setting left in place), the site is indexed but nothing on it matches what people search for, or it competes for terms far above its current authority. Search Console usually distinguishes these quickly, which is why an audit starts there.",
148 "It matters most where it affects people. Core Web Vitals are a real but modest ranking input; the larger commercial effect is that slow pages lose visitors before they read anything, particularly on mobile connections. We treat speed as a build standard rather than a late optimisation pass.",
154 "Any rebuild carries some risk and nobody can honestly guarantee rankings. We reduce the risk by mapping existing URLs to their new equivalents with redirects, carrying over content that already performs, preserving metadata and structured data, and checking indexing after launch.",
163 "Launch is a measurement point, not the end of the work. The production site is verified, measurement is connected, and ownership of accounts and access is agreed. From there a Growth Partnership can continue the work, it can start after a ScaleSmiths build or with an existing website, and it covers agreed priorities rather than an open-ended retainer.",
169 "The proposal defines it. A Growth Partnership can include hosting, updates, monitoring, fixes, SEO, conversion work, content, automation and roadmap delivery, with priorities and working cadence agreed up front. Maintenance protects dependable operation; SEO, content, design changes and new integrations are improvement work and are scoped accordingly.",
175 "Often, after an initial review. We need to understand its code, hosting, access and update path before accepting responsibility, and that review may identify prerequisite repair work or a platform that needs its original specialist. We will not take on an unknown system blind.",
181 "Only where the agreement says so. Routine edits, new pages and campaign work can be included or scoped separately depending on the working model, so the boundary is written into the partnership rather than assumed. If you expect frequent changes, say so during scoping, it affects both the build and the support arrangement.",
186 "Yes, if it is going to work. Search results, competitors and your own services all change, so content, technical health and measurement need continued attention. That is why SEO sits in a Growth Partnership as prioritised improvement work rather than being treated as a task that completes at launch.",
192 "For clients under an agreed arrangement, the escalation route, contacts and cadence are documented as part of the partnership, and ScaleSmiths can perform emergency maintenance and proportionate protective action. Response commitments exist only where they have been contracted, we do not publish response times we have not agreed with you. If you need emergency help without an existing arrangement, contact us and we will tell you honestly whether we can assist.",
198 "Uptime checks and monitoring are part of managed hosting and maintenance arrangements, scoped to the actual stack. What is monitored, and what happens when a check fails, is written into the agreement rather than implied.",
204 "Not automatically. Hosting can be part of a Growth Partnership or arranged as a managed hosting service on its own, and the order states which applications, environments, monitoring, maintenance and backups are covered. Managed Business Email is likewise separate unless a combined arrangement is written into the agreement.",
210 "A Growth Partnership works to an agreed roadmap and a prioritised backlog rather than a first-come queue, so work that matters commercially is not displaced by whatever arrived most recently. Incidents affecting a live service take precedence over improvement work. Clients can raise and track requests through the ScaleSmiths client portal.",
215 "Yes. New features are improvement work: they are specified, scoped and placed on the roadmap rather than absorbed into routine maintenance. Building in phases is a deliberate part of how we work, the first release is dependable, and later work follows evidence rather than a fixed wish list.",
222 "It is the part of a website a template cannot do: booking and quote workflows, integrations with the tools you already use, admin areas, databases, user roles, and hosting that someone is accountable for. Published examples include the CSDS multi-step quote form feeding its own admin panel, and the Glow Tanning booking and review integrations behind an admin login.",
228 "Software built around one organisation's workflow instead of configured from a general-purpose product. It is justified when the workflow genuinely differentiates the business, when existing tools create material friction, or when integration and data-ownership needs cannot be met by configuration. If a proven product already meets the requirement, buying and integrating it is usually the better decision, and we will say so.",
234 "Yes, where an off-the-shelf CRM does not fit the workflow. Confirm-A-Kill runs on a private PostgreSQL-backed CRM covering enquiries, customers, properties, quotations, appointments, jobs, visits and commercial service records; CSDS has a quote management admin panel behind its website. If an existing CRM already does the job, connecting the website to it is often the better investment.",
241 "Yes. ScaleSmiths runs its own client portal for projects, invoices, documents, messages and requests, with tenant isolation enforced server-side. The Business Circle is a published membership platform with tiered access, and VeteranFinder includes member and admin applications. Permissions and tenant boundaries are enforced on the server rather than treated as interface options.",
247 "Yes. The Business Circle runs Stripe subscription billing for tiered memberships, and Prymal uses Stripe for plans, team seats and execution credits. Card details stay with the payment provider === we do not create a reason to handle them directly === and order or subscription state relies on verified server-side provider events rather than a browser redirect alone.",
252 "Usually, yes. Published work includes a Salon Tracker booking integration and Google and Facebook review aggregation for Glow Tanning, and Stripe subscription billing with LiveKit video for The Business Circle. We check the existing system's API, data and ownership before committing to an approach, because not every tool exposes what an integration needs.",
257 "Yes, starting with one bounded workflow whose owner, inputs, exceptions and useful outcome can be defined. Useful automation removes repeated handling while preserving the decisions people still need to make, so high-consequence steps keep a human review point and a record of what the system proposed or changed. Deterministic rules and integrations are often safer and cheaper than adding a language model; AI is used where interpretation is genuinely required.",
263 "Yes, and usually gradually. A phased system can begin with the highest-friction workflow and leave stable existing processes in place until replacement is justified. That avoids the common failure of rebuilding everything at once and discovering the exceptions afterwards.",
269 "Yes. Admin surfaces are a recurring part of published work: quote management for CSDS, product and catalogue administration for Pinkys Prints, content administration for Glow Tanning, member management for The Business Circle, and a dedicated admin console for VeteranFinder. Roles, permissions and sensitive operations are enforced server-side.",
275 "That is the point of building it deliberately. We define a release boundary rather than a wish list, keep data and permissions designed for the next stage, and document deployment and operations as part of delivery. Later phases then extend a system that is understood, instead of working around one nobody can safely change.",
280 "Yes. We separate the essential launch scope from later improvements, so the first release is dependable and further work follows evidence rather than a fixed wish list.",
287 "Yes. ScaleSmiths Managed Business Email starts at £15 per month for three custom-domain mailboxes with 5GB of storage each, and initial mailbox and DNS setup is included at no additional setup charge. It covers webmail, desktop and mobile client compatibility, aliases and forwarding, spam filtering, TLS-secured transport, and SPF, DKIM and DMARC configuration. It is available standalone, you do not need a ScaleSmiths website.",
293 "Sender Policy Framework is a DNS record listing which mail servers are allowed to send email using your domain. When a receiving system gets a message claiming to be from you, it checks that record to see whether the sending server is on the list. Without it, anyone can send mail that appears to come from your domain, and legitimate mail is more likely to be treated as suspicious.",
299 "DomainKeys Identified Mail adds a cryptographic signature to the messages you send, using a key published in your DNS. The receiving system verifies that signature to confirm the message really came from your domain and was not altered in transit. SPF establishes where mail was sent from; DKIM establishes that it has not been tampered with.",
305 "DMARC ties SPF and DKIM together. It tells receiving mail systems what to do when a message fails those checks === monitor, quarantine or reject it === and can send reports back so you can see who is sending mail as your domain. It is the policy layer that makes the other two records meaningful.",
311 "Most often because the domain's authentication records are missing or wrong, so receiving systems cannot verify the mail is genuinely yours. Sending from a free consumer address, a shared or poor-reputation server, or a domain with no sending history makes it worse. Correct SPF, DKIM and DMARC configuration supports good deliverability, but no configuration can guarantee that every message reaches an inbox.",
317 "Yes, where you give us appropriate access. Managed Business Email onboarding includes configuring the required mail and authentication records, and website or hosting work includes the DNS changes a launch or migration needs. We use delegated or scoped access where it is supported, and we never ask for domain or registrar passwords through a public form.",
322 "You remain the registrant unless a transfer is expressly agreed in writing. ScaleSmiths needs appropriate access to configure records, but a domain transfer is not automatically required. If you want us to take on registration or renewal administration, ask and we will scope it explicitly rather than assume it.",
327 "Yes. HTTPS is a build standard, not an upsell, and certificate provisioning and renewal are part of managed hosting and deployment. The specific arrangement depends on where the site runs: platform-managed certificates on a host such as Vercel, or certificates managed at the Nginx layer on a VPS deployment.",
333 "Backups are part of a managed hosting or maintenance arrangement, and the order states which environments, data and retention are covered. We are deliberately plain about the limits: backups reduce risk but do not make loss impossible, they do not replace your own continuity responsibilities, and no restoration guarantee, recovery point or recovery time is created by our online terms. Ask, and the actual arrangement is written into the agreement.",
339 "It depends on the build. Published work runs on self-hosted Docker Compose and Nginx deployments on a VPS, and on managed platforms such as Vercel. We choose around the workload, operational risk and support model rather than defaulting to one provider, and the hosting arrangement is documented so nobody is guessing who is accountable.",
347 "Published starting prices are website design and development from £2,000, a Growth Partnership from £350 per month, the Business Growth Audit at £395, and managed business email from £15 per month. A starting price is the entry point for an agreed scope. It is not unlimited development, marketing, support or a guaranteed outcome. The final price follows a written proposal based on requirements, complexity and the deliverables we agree. Custom software is scoped after discovery and is not sold as one of those starting prices.",
353 "Payment terms, including any staged or upfront payment, are set out in the proposal and signed order for each project rather than published as a blanket policy. Ownership of bespoke deliverables transfers once the applicable agreed fees are paid. Ask during discovery and you will have the terms in writing before anything is committed.",
358 "Yes. ScaleSmiths is based in Hucknall, Nottinghamshire and works with businesses across the UK. Published work also includes CSDS, a computer repair firm in Pennsylvania. Projects outside the area, including work with businesses overseas, run remotely with a review cadence agreed in the scope. We do not claim overseas offices or regional expertise we cannot substantiate. Proposals are quoted in GBP.",
363 "The founders review what you send and reply with a sensible next step. That may be a few clarifying questions, a recommendation to start with the Business Growth Audit, or a proposal once the scope is understood. Sending the form does not take payment and does not create a contract. The quote, audit and email journeys each say what happens next on their own confirmation pages.",
368 "We agree which signals are worth watching for that business, such as enquiries, calls, Search Console and analytics where you can give access, and we review them in conversation rather than against invented targets. Confirm-A-Kill shows the pattern: a recorded pre-launch baseline, then post-launch measurement that is still being monitored. We do not publish a universal KPI or a guaranteed lift.",
373 "Yes, where the scope is honest about the stage. Published work includes early platforms such as The Business Circle, Prymal and VeteranFinder. For an early-stage business we would usually argue for a bounded first release that tests the commercial idea, rather than a full platform built before anyone has established that people want it.",
378 "Yes, and that is where most of the client work sits. Confirm-A-Kill is an established Nottinghamshire pest-control business whose website and operating systems were rebuilt around search, conversion and day-to-day delivery. Established businesses usually have real evidence === rankings, enquiries, existing systems === and the work starts by protecting what already performs.",
384 "Usually, yes, but never sight unseen. We start with a code and infrastructure review so the path forward is based on what is actually there, and that review sometimes concludes that finishing the existing build would cost more than replacing part of it. You get that assessment honestly, before committing to delivery.",
389 "Ownership or licence of the bespoke deliverable follows the signed project documents, and any transfer occurs once the applicable agreed fees are paid. Clients retain their own materials, trademarks and business data. ScaleSmiths retains its pre-existing tools, frameworks, methods and know-how, and third-party and open-source components stay under their own licences. It is written down rather than left to assumption.",
394 "Yes. We can take a defined delivery stream, unblock architecture decisions, or build alongside an existing marketing or operations team. Where an audit produces a roadmap, your own team or another supplier is welcome to implement it, the findings are useful either way.",

# Operation Empower: B1 planning package

**Package status: DRAFT. Nothing in this folder is approved, published or available to partners or clients.**

Operation Empower prepares two partner capabilities for engineering:

- the **Partner Academy**, an optional, voluntary learning area inside the Partner Portal; and
- the **Sales Resource Centre**, an approved-content library and knowledge base that partners search before speaking to a prospect.

This is B1 research, architecture and content design only. It changes no application code, migrations, authentication, CI or production systems. Implementation must not start until B0 ([PR #155](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/155), branch `claude/modest-newton-jo2d95`) is merged. Its readiness record is [B0-MERGE-READINESS.md](../intelligence/B0-MERGE-READINESS.md).

## Contents

| Document | What it holds |
|---|---|
| [PLATFORM-AUDIT.md](PLATFORM-AUDIT.md) | The existing systems Empower reuses, with file references and gaps |
| [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) | Proposed data model, content lifecycle, deterministic search and integration points |
| [SECURITY-MODEL.md](SECURITY-MODEL.md) | Roles, audience separation, publication controls, threats and mitigations |
| [CURRICULUM.md](CURRICULUM.md) | The 13 Academy courses: objectives, modules, lesson outlines, knowledge checks, resources and review requirements |
| [LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md](LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md) | Initial lesson content, courses 1 to 6 (company and services) |
| [LESSONS-PRACTICE.md](LESSONS-PRACTICE.md) | Initial lesson content, courses 7 to 13 (selling, policy and conduct) |
| [resources/README.md](resources/README.md) | The 13 Resource Centre drafts, one file each |
| [KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md](KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md) | Approved-content architecture and the knowledge article inventory |
| [DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md](DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md) | Visual language, tokens and components, reconciled with the existing design systems |
| [WIREFRAMES.md](WIREFRAMES.md) | Wireframe descriptions for the seven key screens |
| [FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md) | Every item in this package with its approval status, owner and blocking effect |
| [IMPLEMENTATION-PHASES.md](IMPLEMENTATION-PHASES.md) | Proposed delivery phases and their entry and exit gates |
| [ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA.md](ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA.md) | Testable acceptance criteria for each phase |

## Status vocabulary

Every item in this package carries one of these labels. The register lists them all.

| Label | Meaning | May a partner use it? |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED` | The wording or figure is already published on the public site from a founder-maintained source in the repository (for example `web/src/lib/published-starting-prices.ts` or `web/src/lib/faq-library.ts`). Empower restates it; it does not create it. | Only once an Academy or resource version containing it is approved and published |
| `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED, OWNER REVIEW` | Published, but the source marks it `ownerReview: true`, so founders should confirm it before it is expanded | No, until confirmed |
| `CONFIRMED: SYSTEM BEHAVIOUR` | A fact about how the software behaves, verified in B0 source. It is not commercial approval | Not on its own |
| `PROPOSED POLICY` | A commercial or legal position that exists in B0 drafts or the draft `/partners` page but is not approved (for example the 30% acquisition commission) | No. Must always be labelled as proposed |
| `DRAFT` | Written in this package. Needs founder review | No |
| `FOUNDER DECISION` | Content cannot be finalised until a founder or adviser decides | No |
| `BLOCKED` | Waiting on an external prerequisite, such as the B0 merge or legal advice | No |

No item in this package is `APPROVED`. That status exists only in the future publishing workflow (see [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)), where a founder records it against an immutable content version.

## Content rules applied throughout

These rules come from the B0 programme sources and the public-site content policy. They apply to every draft here and to every future edit.

1. **No guaranteed outcomes.** No ranking, traffic, enquiry, revenue or earnings guarantees. The source position is published at `faq-library.ts` (`ranking-guarantees`) and on `/partners` ("No guaranteed earnings").
2. **No invented proof.** No testimonials, quotes, statistics or client names beyond the published work listed in `web/src/lib/data.ts`. Partner reuse of published case studies still needs founder permission (see [CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](../intelligence/CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md)).
3. **Prices are the published starting prices only**: website from £2,000, Growth Partnership from £350 per month, Business Growth Audit £395, business email from £15 per month. Always paired with the starting-price boundary (`STARTING_PRICE_BOUNDARY`). GBP only.
4. **Commission and rewards are proposed, never promised.** Figures in `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts` are illustrations of the proposed programme. Every plan is disabled by default and no reward is payable.
5. **Independence is preserved.** The Academy is optional and voluntary, as the programme states. No course is compulsory and no completion affects commission, allocation or standing. An employment solicitor should confirm this (register item `AP-GOV-02`).
6. **Partner-only and client-facing material are kept apart.** Client-facing material never contains commission, founder-only or internal information.
7. **Escalate rather than improvise.** Where an answer depends on scope, contract or technical review, the content says so and names the escalation route.

## Relationship to existing registers

This package extends, and does not replace, the B0 registers:

- [FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md](../intelligence/FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md): commercial, legal and operational decisions;
- [CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](../intelligence/CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md): content not yet written (much of which this package now drafts);
- [COMMERCIAL-ACTIVATION-GATES.md](../hardening/COMMERCIAL-ACTIVATION-GATES.md): release modes and gates.

When the founders approve an Empower item, record it in [FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md) and, where it resolves a row there, in the matching B0 register.

## Status vocabulary

Every item in this package carries one of these labels. The register lists them all.

| Label | Meaning | May a partner use it? |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED` | The wording or figure is already published on the public site from a founder-maintained source in the repository (for example `web/src/lib/published-starting-prices.ts` or `web/src/lib/faq-library.ts`). Empower restates it; it does not create it. | Only once an Academy or resource version containing it is approved and published |
| `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED, OWNER REVIEW` | Published, but the source marks it `ownerReview: true`, so founders should confirm it before it is expanded | No, until confirmed |
| `CONFIRMED: SYSTEM BEHAVIOUR` | A fact about how the software behaves, verified in B0 source. It is not commercial approval | Not on its own |
| `PROPOSED POLICY` | A commercial or legal position that exists in B0 drafts or the draft `/partners` page but is not approved (for example the 30% acquisition commission) | No. Must always be labelled as proposed |
| `DRAFT` | Written in this package. Needs founder review | No |
| `FOUNDER DECISION` | Content cannot be finalised until a founder or adviser decides | No |
| `BLOCKED` | Waiting on an external prerequisite, such as the B0 merge or legal advice | No |

No item in this package is `APPROVED`. That status exists only in the future publishing workflow (see [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)), where a founder records it against an immutable content version.

## Content rules applied throughout

These rules come from the B0 programme sources and the public-site content policy. They apply to every draft here and to every future edit.

1. **No guaranteed outcomes.** No ranking, traffic, enquiry, revenue or earnings guarantees. The source position is published at `faq-library.ts` (`ranking-guarantees`) and on `/partners` ("No guaranteed earnings").
2. **No invented proof.** No testimonials, quotes, statistics or client names beyond the published work listed in `web/src/lib/data.ts`. Partner reuse of published case studies still needs founder permission (see [CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](../intelligence/CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md)).

5. **Independence is preserved.** The Academy is optional and voluntary, as the programme states. No course is compulsory and no completion affects commission, allocation or standing. An employment solicitor should confirm this (register item `AP-GOV-02`).
6. **Partner-only and client-facing material are kept apart.** Client-facing material never contains commission, founder-only or internal information.
