input.content:
# Partner Academy curriculum

**Status: DRAFT. No course is approved, published or available.** Initial lesson content is in [LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md](LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md) (courses 1 to 6) and [LESSONS-PRACTICE.md](LESSONS-PRACTICE.md) (courses 7 to 13).

## Principles

- **Optional and voluntary.** The programme describes the Academy as optional and voluntary (`FEATURE_AVAILABILITY` in `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts`). There are no compulsory courses, deadlines, scores, certificates, rankings or completion targets, and completion never affects commission, allocation, recognition or standing. Wording is "you may find it useful", never "you must". Solicitor review: `AP-GOV-02`.
- **Approved sources only.** Each lesson lists its sources. Where a source is a draft or a proposal, the lesson says so in the text.
- **Teach the boundary, not just the pitch.** Each service course has a lesson on what the service is *not*, and when to escalate.
- **Short lessons.** Five to ten minutes each, readable on a phone.
- **Knowledge checks are optional self-checks.** Answers are shown immediately and nothing is stored except "attempted".

## Course map

| # | Course | Modules | Lessons | Audience of content | Review owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C01 | Welcome to ScaleSmiths | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C02 | Professional Website Development | 3 | 8 | Partner only (includes client-safe phrasing) | Delivery founder | `DRAFT` |
| C03 | SEO and Digital Growth | 3 | 8 | Partner only | Delivery founder | `DRAFT` |
| C04 | Growth Partnerships | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C05 | Website Migration | 2 | 6 | Partner only | Delivery founder | `DRAFT` |
| C06 | Bespoke Software and Automation | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Delivery founder | `DRAFT` |
| C07 | Finding Prospects | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Founders + privacy adviser | `DRAFT`, `BLOCKED` (marketing process) |
| C08 | Discovery Meetings | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C09 | Presenting ScaleSmiths | 3 | 6 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C10 | Objection Handling | 3 | 8 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C11 | Commercial Policies | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Founders + accountant + solicitor | `DRAFT`, `BLOCKED` (agreement, terms) |
| C12 | Professional Conduct | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Founders + employment solicitor | `DRAFT`, `BLOCKED` (agreement) |
| C13 | Advanced and Enterprise Opportunities | 3 | 6 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |

Suggested (not required) order: C01, C12, C02, C04, C08, then any.

---

## C01 Welcome to ScaleSmiths

**Purpose:** a clear, honest picture of who ScaleSmiths is, what it sells and how the partnership works.

**Learning objectives.** After this course a partner can:
1. describe ScaleSmiths and its services in two sentences without overstating them;
2. explain what an independent partner does and does not do;
3. find approved answers in the Resource Centre and know when to ask for help;
4. tell the difference between approved, proposed and planned features.

**Modules and lessons**

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Who we are | C01-L1 The ScaleSmiths story in plain words | Based in Hucknall, Nottinghamshire; custom builds; published work; how to say it briefly |
| | C01-L2 What we sell | Four published offers plus independently scoped custom work; starting-price boundary |
| | C01-L3 How we work | Discovery, written proposal, phased delivery, evidence over promises |
| M2 Your role | C01-L4 What an independent partner does | Introduce, qualify, register, support; ScaleSmiths scopes, prices and delivers |
| | C01-L5 What is live, proposed and planned | Reading the availability labels; why nothing is promised |
| M3 Using the portal | C01-L6 Finding answers fast | Knowledge search, resources, approval ribbons, versions |
| | C01-L7 Getting help | Meeting types, escalation, what to send |

**Optional knowledge check:** five questions (for example "A prospect asks whether we guarantee first place on Google. What is the approved answer?").

**Supporting resources:** [R01 Company brochure](resources/R01-company-brochure.md), [R02 Partner handbook](resources/R02-partner-handbook.md), knowledge entries `KB-COM-01`, `KB-ONB-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** confirm company description and service list (`AP-CNT-01`); confirm the partner role wording matches the final agreement (`AP-GOV-01`); confirm the availability labels at review time.

---

## C02 Professional Website Development

**Purpose:** explain ScaleSmiths website projects accurately and recognise a good-fit prospect.

**Learning objectives:**
1. explain what a typical website project includes and excludes;
2. state the published starting price with its boundary;
3. explain hosting, domains, ownership and self-editing at a client-friendly level;
4. recognise when a project is really custom software, e-commerce or migration and route it.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 The offer | C02-L1 What a website project includes | Messaging, structure, responsive build, search foundations, enquiry route, launch support |
| | C02-L2 What is separate | Hosting, ongoing SEO, content programmes, integrations, open-ended support |
| | C02-L3 Price and proposal | "From £2,000" and the starting-price boundary; the proposal is the scope |
| M2 Questions clients ask | C02-L4 Timelines | Confirmed after discovery; content readiness drives schedule |
| | C02-L5 Ownership and editing | Ownership follows signed documents and payment; editing is a scoping decision |
| | C02-L6 Technology and WordPress | Custom builds; WordPress is reviewed on its merits (owner review flag) |
| M3 Fit and routing | C02-L7 Good-fit signals | Established business, clear services, evidence to protect |
| | C02-L8 When it is not a standard website | E-commerce, booking, portals, migration → escalate |

**Optional knowledge check:** six questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R03 Website development guide](resources/R03-website-development-guide.md), [R11 Commercial pricing reference](resources/R11-commercial-pricing-reference.md), `KB-HOST-*`, `KB-DOM-*`, `KB-ECOM-01`, `KB-BOOK-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** confirm "what is included" list; confirm WordPress wording (source is `ownerReview`); approve use of published project names in partner conversations (`AP-PROOF-01`).

---

## C03 SEO and Digital Growth

**Purpose:** talk about search visibility, including AI search, accurately and without promises.

**Learning objectives:**
1. explain SEO, local SEO and technical SEO in plain language;
2. explain what is included in a build and what is ongoing work;
3. explain AI search (answer engines) honestly, without claiming control over it;
4. respond to "can you guarantee page one?" with the approved answer.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Foundations | C03-L1 What SEO is | Technical, content, on-page experience; ongoing work |
| | C03-L2 Local SEO | Area searches, consistent details, Google Business Profile, local proof |
| | C03-L3 Technical SEO | Crawl, render, canonicals, sitemaps, redirects, Core Web Vitals, HTTPS |
| M2 Honest expectations | C03-L4 Timescales and guarantees | Months, not weeks; no position is promised |
| | C03-L5 Build versus ongoing | Foundations in build; ongoing via project or Growth Partnership |
| | C03-L6 SEO and paid search | Different problems; honest recommendation |
| M3 AI search | C03-L7 What AI search and AEO mean | Answer engines, structured content, direct answers; no guarantee of inclusion |
| | C03-L8 Diagnosing "not on Google" | Indexing, intent mismatch, authority; why audits start in Search Console |

**Optional knowledge check:** six questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R06 SEO and AEO guide](resources/R06-seo-and-aeo-guide.md), `KB-SEO-*`, `KB-AIS-*`, `KB-ANL-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** approve the AI search lesson (no published FAQ answer exists yet; `AP-CNT-06`); confirm Business Growth Audit positioning.

---

## C04 Growth Partnerships

**Purpose:** explain the Growth Partnership as a scoped, ongoing service, not an unlimited retainer.

**Learning objectives:**
1. explain what a Growth Partnership can include and how scope is agreed;
2. state the published starting price and its boundary;
3. explain how requests are prioritised;
4. explain that it can follow a ScaleSmiths build or start with an existing site.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 The service | C04-L1 What a Growth Partnership is | SEO, conversion, content, analytics, automation, technical support; scoped |
| | C04-L2 What it is not | Not unlimited; not only maintenance; not a guarantee |
| | C04-L3 Price and term | From £350/month published; any minimum term is a proposal-level term (programme `standard-v2` twelve-month term is `PROPOSED POLICY`) |
| M2 How it runs | C04-L4 Roadmap and priorities | Agreed roadmap, incidents first, client portal requests |
| | C04-L5 Hosting, email and monitoring | Included only when the order says so |
| M3 Positioning | C04-L6 After a build | Launch as a measurement point |
| | C04-L7 Existing websites | Review before responsibility |

**Optional knowledge check:** five questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R04 Growth Partnership guide](resources/R04-growth-partnership-guide.md), `KB-GP-*`, `KB-HOST-02`.

**Founder review requirements:** decide whether a minimum term is offered to clients and how partners describe it (`AP-COM-03`); confirm suitability criteria for Growth-Partnership-only clients (B0 open decision).

---

## C05 Website Migration

**Purpose:** recognise migration opportunities and explain the risk honestly.

**Learning objectives:**
1. explain what a migration involves (platform, hosting, URLs, data);
2. explain how search risk is reduced and why it cannot be removed;
3. identify the information needed before a migration can be scoped;
4. escalate every migration for technical review.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Understanding migration | C05-L1 Types of migration | Platform rebuild, hosting move, domain change, CMS change |
| | C05-L2 WordPress and Shopify moves | Review what works first; Pinkys Prints as published example |
| | C05-L3 Redirects and search risk | URL mapping, metadata, internal links, post-launch indexing checks |
| M2 Preparing a referral | C05-L4 What to collect | Access, current URLs, analytics, integrations, licences |
| | C05-L5 Red flags | Unknown hosting, no access, expiring domain, unlicensed plugins |
| | C05-L6 Escalation | Always a technical scoping request |

**Optional knowledge check:** five questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R03 Website development guide](resources/R03-website-development-guide.md), [R10 Technical escalation guide](resources/R10-technical-escalation-guide.md), `KB-MIG-*`, `KB-RED-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** confirm migration wording (source `seo-rebuild` is `ownerReview`); approve the "red flags" list.

---

## C06 Bespoke Software and Automation

**Purpose:** spot genuine custom-software needs and avoid overselling them.

**Learning objectives:**
1. explain when custom software is justified and when buying a product is better;
2. describe published examples of CRMs, portals, admin systems and integrations accurately;
3. explain phased delivery;
4. explain the ScaleSmiths position on automation and AI (deterministic first, human review on high-consequence steps).

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 When custom makes sense | C06-L1 Custom versus off the shelf | Differentiating workflow, friction, integration, data ownership |
| | C06-L2 What we have built | CRMs, portals, admin systems, payments, integrations (published examples only) |
| M2 Automation | C06-L3 Automating a workflow | One bounded workflow, human review points |
| | C06-L4 Spreadsheets and manual processes | Gradual replacement |
| | C06-L5 AI, honestly | Used where interpretation is required; not by default |
| M3 Selling it well | C06-L6 Phases and scoping | Release boundary, discovery, never priced against a website starting price |
| | C06-L7 Bespoke discovery requests | When to request a `bespoke_discovery` meeting |

**Optional knowledge check:** five questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R05 Bespoke software guide](resources/R05-bespoke-software-guide.md), `KB-CRM-01`, `KB-SW-*`, `KB-AUTO-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** confirm CRM wording (`ownerReview`); approve bespoke eligibility description (B0 open decision "Bespoke eligibility, existing-customer attribution").

---

## C07 Finding Prospects

**Purpose:** find suitable businesses lawfully and respectfully.

**Status note:** `BLOCKED`. The marketing process (permitted channels, screening, opt-out handling, training) is an open founder and privacy-adviser decision and "unsolicited outreach" stays on hold until approved ([COMMERCIAL-ACTIVATION-GATES.md](../hardening/COMMERCIAL-ACTIVATION-GATES.md)). Lessons C07-L4 and C07-L5 cannot be finalised until then.

**Learning objectives:**
1. describe a good-fit prospect;
2. use your own network and introductions appropriately;
3. understand registration, lead protection and duplicates at a high level;
4. understand that direct marketing has legal rules and follow the approved process.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|

# Partner Academy curriculum

**Status: DRAFT. No course is approved, published or available.** Initial lesson content is in [LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md](LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md) (courses 1 to 6) and [LESSONS-PRACTICE.md](LESSONS-PRACTICE.md) (courses 7 to 13).

## Principles

- **Optional and voluntary.** The programme describes the Academy as optional and voluntary (`FEATURE_AVAILABILITY` in `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts`). There are no compulsory courses, deadlines, scores, certificates, rankings or completion targets, and completion never affects commission, allocation, recognition or standing. Wording is "you may find it useful", never "you must". Solicitor review: `AP-GOV-02`.
- **Approved sources only.** Each lesson lists its sources. Where a source is a draft or a proposal, the lesson says so in the text.
- **Teach the boundary, not just the pitch.** Each service course has a lesson on what the service is *not*, and when to escalate.
- **Short lessons.** Five to ten minutes each, readable on a phone.
- **Knowledge checks are optional self-checks.** Answers are shown immediately and nothing is stored except "attempted".

## Course map

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**Learning objectives.** After this course a partner can:

# Partner Academy curriculum

**Status: DRAFT. No course is approved, published or available.** Initial lesson content is in [LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md](LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md) (courses 1 to 6) and [LESSONS-PRACTICE.md](LESSONS-PRACTICE.md) (courses 7 to 13).

## Principles

- **Optional and voluntary.** The programme describes the Academy as optional and voluntary (`FEATURE_AVAILABILITY` in `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts`). There are no compulsory courses, deadlines, scores, certificates, rankings or completion targets, and completion never affects commission, allocation, recognition or standing. Wording is "you may find it useful", never "you must". Solicitor review: `AP-GOV-02`.
- **Approved sources only.** Each lesson lists its sources. Where a source is a draft or a proposal, the lesson says so in the text.
- **Teach the boundary, not just the pitch.** Each service course has a lesson on what the service is *not*, and when to escalate.
- **Short lessons.** Five to ten minutes each, readable on a phone.
- **Knowledge checks are optional self-checks.** Answers are shown immediately and nothing is stored except "attempted".

## Course map

| # | Course | Modules | Lessons | Audience of content | Review owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C01 | Welcome to ScaleSmiths | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C02 | Professional Website Development | 3 | 8 | Partner only (includes client-safe phrasing) | Delivery founder | `DRAFT` |
| C03 | SEO and Digital Growth | 3 | 8 | Partner only | Delivery founder | `DRAFT` |
| C04 | Growth Partnerships | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C05 | Website Migration | 2 | 6 | Partner only | Delivery founder | `DRAFT` |
| C06 | Bespoke Software and Automation | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Delivery founder | `DRAFT` |
| C07 | Finding Prospects | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Founders + privacy adviser | `DRAFT`, `BLOCKED` (marketing process) |
| C08 | Discovery Meetings | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C09 | Presenting ScaleSmiths | 3 | 6 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C10 | Objection Handling | 3 | 8 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C11 | Commercial Policies | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Founders + accountant + solicitor | `DRAFT`, `BLOCKED` (agreement, terms) |
| C12 | Professional Conduct | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Founders + employment solicitor | `DRAFT`, `BLOCKED` (agreement) |
| C13 | Advanced and Enterprise Opportunities | 3 | 6 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |

Suggested (not required) order: C01, C12, C02, C04, C08, then any.

---

## C01 Welcome to ScaleSmiths

**Purpose:** a clear, honest picture of who ScaleSmiths is, what it sells and how the partnership works.

**Learning objectives.** After this course a partner can:
1. describe ScaleSmiths and its services in two sentences without overstating them;
2. explain what an independent partner does and does not do;
3. find approved answers in the Resource Centre and know when to ask for help;
4. tell the difference between approved, proposed and planned features.

**Modules and lessons**

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Who we are | C01-L1 The ScaleSmiths story in plain words | Based in Hucknall, Nottinghamshire; custom builds; published work; how to say it briefly |
| | C01-L2 What we sell | Four published offers plus independently scoped custom work; starting-price boundary |
| | C01-L3 How we work | Discovery, written proposal, phased delivery, evidence over promises |
| M2 Your role | C01-L4 What an independent partner does | Introduce, qualify, register, support; ScaleSmiths scopes, prices and delivers |
| | C01-L5 What is live, proposed and planned | Reading the availability labels; why nothing is promised |
| M3 Using the portal | C01-L6 Finding answers fast | Knowledge search, resources, approval ribbons, versions |
| | C01-L7 Getting help | Meeting types, escalation, what to send |

**Optional knowledge check:** five questions (for example "A prospect asks whether we guarantee first place on Google. What is the approved answer?").

**Supporting resources:** [R01 Company brochure](resources/R01-company-brochure.md), [R02 Partner handbook](resources/R02-partner-handbook.md), knowledge entries `KB-COM-01`, `KB-ONB-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** confirm company description and service list (`AP-CNT-01`); confirm the partner role wording matches the final agreement (`AP-GOV-01`); confirm the availability labels at review time.

---

## C02 Professional Website Development

**Purpose:** explain ScaleSmiths website projects accurately and recognise a good-fit prospect.

**Learning objectives:**
1. explain what a typical website project includes and excludes;
2. state the published starting price with its boundary;
3. explain hosting, domains, ownership and self-editing at a client-friendly level;
4. recognise when a project is really custom software, e-commerce or migration and route it.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 The offer | C02-L1 What a website project includes | Messaging, structure, responsive build, search foundations, enquiry route, launch support |
| | C02-L2 What is separate | Hosting, ongoing SEO, content programmes, integrations, open-ended support |
| | C02-L3 Price and proposal | "From £2,000" and the starting-price boundary; the proposal is the scope |
| M2 Questions clients ask | C02-L4 Timelines | Confirmed after discovery; content readiness drives schedule |
| | C02-L5 Ownership and editing | Ownership follows signed documents and payment; editing is a scoping decision |
| | C02-L6 Technology and WordPress | Custom builds; WordPress is reviewed on its merits (owner review flag) |
| M3 Fit and routing | C02-L7 Good-fit signals | Established business, clear services, evidence to protect |
| | C02-L8 When it is not a standard website | E-commerce, booking, portals, migration → escalate |

**Optional knowledge check:** six questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R03 Website development guide](resources/R03-website-development-guide.md), [R11 Commercial pricing reference](resources/R11-commercial-pricing-reference.md), `KB-HOST-*`, `KB-DOM-*`, `KB-ECOM-01`, `KB-BOOK-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** confirm "what is included" list; confirm WordPress wording (source is `ownerReview`); approve use of published project names in partner conversations (`AP-PROOF-01`).

---

## C03 SEO and Digital Growth

**Purpose:** talk about search visibility, including AI search, accurately and without promises.

**Learning objectives:**
1. explain SEO, local SEO and technical SEO in plain language;
2. explain what is included in a build and what is ongoing work;
3. explain AI search (answer engines) honestly, without claiming control over it;
4. respond to "can you guarantee page one?" with the approved answer.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Foundations | C03-L1 What SEO is | Technical, content, on-page experience; ongoing work |
| | C03-L2 Local SEO | Area searches, consistent details, Google Business Profile, local proof |
| | C03-L3 Technical SEO | Crawl, render, canonicals, sitemaps, redirects, Core Web Vitals, HTTPS |
| M2 Honest expectations | C03-L4 Timescales and guarantees | Months, not weeks; no position is promised |
| | C03-L5 Build versus ongoing | Foundations in build; ongoing via project or Growth Partnership |
| | C03-L6 SEO and paid search | Different problems; honest recommendation |
| M3 AI search | C03-L7 What AI search and AEO mean | Answer engines, structured content, direct answers; no guarantee of inclusion |
| | C03-L8 Diagnosing "not on Google" | Indexing, intent mismatch, authority; why audits start in Search Console |

**Optional knowledge check:** six questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R06 SEO and AEO guide](resources/R06-seo-and-aeo-guide.md), `KB-SEO-*`, `KB-AIS-*`, `KB-ANL-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** approve the AI search lesson (no published FAQ answer exists yet; `AP-CNT-06`); confirm Business Growth Audit positioning.

---

## C04 Growth Partnerships

**Purpose:** explain the Growth Partnership as a scoped, ongoing service, not an unlimited retainer.

**Learning objectives:**
1. explain what a Growth Partnership can include and how scope is agreed;
2. state the published starting price and its boundary;
3. explain how requests are prioritised;
4. explain that it can follow a ScaleSmiths build or start with an existing site.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 The service | C04-L1 What a Growth Partnership is | SEO, conversion, content, analytics, automation, technical support; scoped |
| | C04-L2 What it is not | Not unlimited; not only maintenance; not a guarantee |
| | C04-L3 Price and term | From £350/month published; any minimum term is a proposal-level term (programme `standard-v2` twelve-month term is `PROPOSED POLICY`) |
| M2 How it runs | C04-L4 Roadmap and priorities | Agreed roadmap, incidents first, client portal requests |
| | C04-L5 Hosting, email and monitoring | Included only when the order says so |
| M3 Positioning | C04-L6 After a build | Launch as a measurement point |
| | C04-L7 Existing websites | Review before responsibility |

**Optional knowledge check:** five questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R04 Growth Partnership guide](resources/R04-growth-partnership-guide.md), `KB-GP-*`, `KB-HOST-02`.

**Founder review requirements:** decide whether a minimum term is offered to clients and how partners describe it (`AP-COM-03`); confirm suitability criteria for Growth-Partnership-only clients (B0 open decision).

---

## C05 Website Migration

**Purpose:** recognise migration opportunities and explain the risk honestly.

**Learning objectives:**
1. explain what a migration involves (platform, hosting, URLs, data);
2. explain how search risk is reduced and why it cannot be removed;
3. identify the information needed before a migration can be scoped;
4. escalate every migration for technical review.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Understanding migration | C05-L1 Types of migration | Platform rebuild, hosting move, domain change, CMS change |
| | C05-L2 WordPress and Shopify moves | Review what works first; Pinkys Prints as published example |
| | C05-L3 Redirects and search risk | URL mapping, metadata, internal links, post-launch indexing checks |
| M2 Preparing a referral | C05-L4 What to collect | Access, current URLs, analytics, integrations, licences |
| | C05-L5 Red flags | Unknown hosting, no access, expiring domain, unlicensed plugins |
| | C05-L6 Escalation | Always a technical scoping request |

**Optional knowledge check:** five questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R03 Website development guide](resources/R03-website-development-guide.md), [R10 Technical escalation guide](resources/R10-technical-escalation-guide.md), `KB-MIG-*`, `KB-RED-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** confirm migration wording (source `seo-rebuild` is `ownerReview`); approve the "red flags" list.

---

## C06 Bespoke Software and Automation

**Purpose:** spot genuine custom-software needs and avoid overselling them.

**Learning objectives:**
1. explain when custom software is justified and when buying a product is better;
2. describe published examples of CRMs, portals, admin systems and integrations accurately;
3. explain phased delivery;
4. explain the ScaleSmiths position on automation and AI (deterministic first, human review on high-consequence steps).

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 When custom makes sense | C06-L1 Custom versus off the shelf | Differentiating workflow, friction, integration, data ownership |
| | C06-L2 What we have built | CRMs, portals, admin systems, payments, integrations (published examples only) |
| M2 Automation | C06-L3 Automating a workflow | One bounded workflow, human review points |
| | C06-L4 Spreadsheets and manual processes | Gradual replacement |
| | C06-L5 AI, honestly | Used where interpretation is required; not by default |
| M3 Selling it well | C06-L6 Phases and scoping | Release boundary, discovery, never priced against a website starting price |
| | C06-L7 Bespoke discovery requests | When to request a `bespoke_discovery` meeting |

**Optional knowledge check:** five questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R05 Bespoke software guide](resources/R05-bespoke-software-guide.md), `KB-CRM-01`, `KB-SW-*`, `KB-AUTO-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** confirm CRM wording (`ownerReview`); approve bespoke eligibility description (B0 open decision "Bespoke eligibility, existing-customer attribution").

## C07 Finding Prospects

**Purpose:** find suitable businesses lawfully and respectfully.

**Status note:** `BLOCKED`. The marketing process (permitted channels, screening, opt-out handling, training) is an open founder and privacy-adviser decision and "unsolicited outreach" stays on hold until approved ([COMMERCIAL-ACTIVATION-GATES.md](../hardening/COMMERCIAL-ACTIVATION-GATES.md)). Lessons C07-L4 and C07-L5 cannot be finalised until then.

**Learning objectives:**
1. describe a good-fit prospect;
2. use your own network and introductions appropriately;
3. understand registration, lead protection and duplicates at a high level;
4. understand that direct marketing has legal rules and follow the approved process.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |

| M1 Who to look for | C07-L1 Good-fit businesses | Established, clear offer, evidence to protect, growth intent |
| | C07-L2 Warm introductions | Your network, referrals, permission |
| M2 Registering | C07-L3 Registering a prospect | Portal registration, duplicates, lead protection (terms pending) |
| | C07-L4 Researched prospects | Allocated research, screening, nothing is guaranteed (planned) |
| M3 Rules | C07-L5 Contact rules | ICO B2B guidance, TPS/CTPS, opt-outs; approved process only |
| | C07-L6 Suppression and objections | What to do when someone says no |
| | C07-L7 Sectors and exclusivity | Generic "commercial checks" notice; why details stay private |

**Optional knowledge check:** four questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R02 Partner handbook](resources/R02-partner-handbook.md), `KB-ONB-02`.

**Founder review requirements:** marketing process (`AP-LEG-03`); lead protection terms (`AP-COM-06`); researched-prospect screening standard.

## C08 Discovery Meetings

**Purpose:** run a first conversation that finds the real problem and sets up an honest next step.

**Learning objectives:**
1. prepare for a meeting with the checklist;
2. ask open questions about goals, evidence, current systems and constraints;
3. avoid quoting or promising in the meeting;
4. hand over to ScaleSmiths with the information it needs.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Before | C08-L1 Preparing | Research the business, its site and its search presence |
| | C08-L2 Setting the agenda | Purpose, time, what happens next |

| | C08-L4 Listening for fit | Signals for website, partnership, audit or custom |
| | C08-L5 What not to say | No prices beyond published starting prices, no timelines, no guarantees |
| M3 After | C08-L6 Writing up | Structured notes in the questionnaire format |
| | C08-L7 Next steps | Audit, quote request, joint meeting or technical scoping |

**Supporting resources:** [R07 Discovery questionnaire](resources/R07-discovery-questionnaire.md), [R09 Meeting preparation checklist](resources/R09-meeting-preparation-checklist.md), [R13 Follow-up templates](resources/R13-follow-up-templates.md).

**Founder review requirements:** approve the questionnaire; decide whether partners may mention the budget options from the public brief.

## C09 Presenting ScaleSmiths

**Purpose:** present ScaleSmiths clearly and accurately, using approved material.

**Learning objectives:**
1. structure a short presentation around the client's problem;
2. use published work as examples without inventing results;
3. present prices with their boundary;
4. close with a clear, non-pressured next step.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Structure | C09-L1 Problem first | Start with what you heard |

| | C09-L4 Proof you must not use | Testimonials, metrics or names not approved |

## C10 Objection Handling

**Purpose:** respond to common concerns honestly, and know when the honest answer is "ScaleSmiths is not the right fit".

**Learning objectives:**
1. use the acknowledge, clarify, answer, confirm pattern;
2. respond to the eight most common objections with approved wording;

**Purpose:** understand how pricing, payment and commission are *proposed* to work, and what is not yet decided.

# Initial lesson content: courses 1 to 6

**Status: DRAFT. Not approved, not published, not for use with partners or clients.** Every lesson needs founder approval before publication (see [FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md)). Lesson structure is in [CURRICULUM.md](CURRICULUM.md).

Conventions:

- **Sources** lists the repository files a lesson relies on. `faq:<key>` means the entry with that key in `web/src/lib/faq-library.ts`.
- **Say it like this** gives client-safe phrasing taken from published wording.
- Text marked *[PROPOSED POLICY]* or *[FOUNDER DECISION]* must keep that label until the decision is recorded.

---

## C01 Welcome to ScaleSmiths

### C01-L1 The ScaleSmiths story in plain words

**Sources:** faq:outside-nottingham, faq:established-businesses, faq:wordpress, `web/src/lib/data.ts`.

ScaleSmiths is a web and software studio based in Hucknall, Nottinghamshire. It works with businesses across the UK and, remotely, with some businesses overseas. Its published work is custom-built: websites and platforms using technologies such as Next.js, React, Astro, Node.js and PostgreSQL rather than WordPress themes.

Most of its client work is with established businesses: organisations that already have customers, a reputation and some evidence (search rankings, enquiries, existing systems) worth protecting. The work usually starts by understanding what already performs before changing anything.

What makes ScaleSmiths different is less about technology and more about honesty and accountability. It writes scope down, it does not promise rankings or results it cannot control, and it says plainly when a cheaper or simpler option would serve the client better.

**Say it like this:** "ScaleSmiths is a Nottinghamshire web and software studio. They build custom websites and systems for established businesses, and they are very clear about what is included and what is not."

**Sources:** faq:website-migration, faq:rebuilds. **Source:** faq:seo-rebuild (*owner review flagged*). Any rebuild carries some search risk and nobody can honestly guarantee rankings. Every migration goes to **technical scoping** before any price or timeline is discussed. Share what you collected in C05-L4.

**Source:** faq:custom-software. ### C06-L2 What we have built

**Sources:** faq:crm (*owner review flagged*), faq:customer-portals, faq:stripe, faq:integrations, faq:internal-admin-systems.

Published examples, described as the FAQ library describes them:

- a private PostgreSQL-backed CRM for Confirm-A-Kill (enquiries, customers, properties, quotations, appointments, jobs, visits);
- a quote management admin behind the CSDS website;
- Stripe subscription billing for The Business Circle; plans, seats and credits for Prymal;
- booking integration and review aggregation for Glow Tanning;
- product and catalogue administration for Pinkys Prints;
- member and admin applications for VeteranFinder;
- ScaleSmiths' own client portal, with tenant isolation enforced on the server.

Describe what was built. Do not quote outcomes, figures or client opinions unless an approved resource contains them (`AP-PROOF-01`).

### C06-L3 Automating a workflow

**Source:** faq:process-automation. Start with one bounded workflow whose owner, inputs, exceptions and useful outcome can be defined. Good automation removes repeated handling while keeping the decisions people still need to make; high-consequence steps keep a human review point and a record.

### C06-L4 Spreadsheets and manual processes

**Source:** faq:replace-spreadsheets. Replace gradually, beginning with the highest-friction workflow. Rebuilding everything at once is the common failure.

### C06-L5 AI, honestly

Deterministic rules and integrations are often safer and cheaper than a language model. AI is used where interpretation is genuinely required. Do not sell "AI" as a feature in itself.

### C06-L6 Phases and scoping

**Sources:** faq:phases, faq:software-scaling, `engagement-models.ts`. Custom work is scoped after discovery and never priced against a website starting price. The first release has a defined boundary; later phases extend a system that is understood.

### C06-L7 Bespoke discovery requests

Request a **bespoke discovery** meeting when the client describes a workflow, system or integration rather than a website. Include: the workflow in the client's words, the people involved, current tools, rough volumes, what goes wrong today, and any deadline. *[PROPOSED POLICY: bespoke commission eligibility and existing-customer attribution are open founder decisions.]*

**Source:** faq:technical-seo. Crawlability and robots rules, canonical URLs, sitemaps, redirects, structured data, heading hierarchy, mobile rendering, Core Web Vitals and HTTPS. It rarely wins attention on its own, but content cannot perform if the technical layer works against it.

2. **Discovery.** What the business sells, who buys, how they choose, what the current site does well, and what evidence exists.
3. **Written proposal.** Scope, deliverables, delivery range and assumptions, and payment terms.
4. **Phased delivery.** A dependable first release; later work follows evidence.
5. **Measurement.** Agreed signals, reviewed in conversation, not invented targets.

### C01-L4 What an independent partner does

**Sources:** `/partners` page copy (`web/src/app/partners/page.tsx`, draft, not approved), [PARTNER-OPERATIONS.md](../intelligence/PARTNER-OPERATIONS.md).

As an independent partner you introduce suitable businesses, have early conversations, register prospects in the Partner Portal and support the relationship. ScaleSmiths scopes, prices, contracts and delivers the work.

You decide how, when and whether you work. There is no salary, guaranteed income, compulsory working hours or sales target. *[PROPOSED POLICY: the final partner agreement defines the relationship. This lesson must be checked against it.]*

You do **not**: issue quotes, agree discounts, promise timelines, sign anything on ScaleSmiths' behalf, or handle client payments.

### C01-L5 What is live, proposed and planned

**Sources:** `FEATURE_AVAILABILITY` in `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts`.

The programme uses four labels: **Available subject to approval**, **Planned**, **In development** and **Not available in this market**. Read them literally:

- *Available subject to approval* means designed but dependent on the final agreement and approvals.
- *Planned* means not built or not operational, with no date.
- *In development* means being built, not yet available.

In the portal, content carries its own status: only approved, published items are shown, each with a version and review date. If you remember something from a conversation that is not in an approved item, it is not policy.

### C01-L6 Finding answers fast

Start with knowledge search. Type the question as the client asked it ("do you do hosting?"). Results show approved answers with three parts: the precise answer for you, a client-friendly explanation you may use, and the limitation. If an entry says **Escalate**, follow the route it names.

Ribbons tell you what you may share: **Client-facing: approved for sharing** or **Partner only: do not share**.

### C01-L7 Getting help

Use a meeting request in the portal. The types are joint sales, technical scoping, bespoke discovery, commercial assistance, proposal review, training and escalation. Give one to five preferred times and your time zone. ScaleSmiths confirms, proposes an alternative or asks for information. Nothing is booked until it is confirmed.

Send: the business name, what they asked, what you have already said, and any deadline the client mentioned.

---

## C02 Professional Website Development

### C02-L1 What a website project includes

**Sources:** faq:website-included, faq:seo-in-build.

A typical project covers agreed messaging, page structure, a responsive build, on-page search foundations (metadata, canonicals, structured data, headings, internal links, indexation controls, page speed) and a route from visitor to enquiry, plus launch support for that scope. **The proposal is the list of what is included.**

### C02-L2 What is separate

Hosting, ongoing SEO, content programmes, integrations and open-ended support are separate unless the proposal includes them. Managed Business Email is separate unless a combined arrangement is written in. This is not a trick; it is what keeps prices honest.

**Say it like this:** "The build includes the search foundations. Ongoing SEO and support are separate, and the proposal spells out exactly what's in."

### C02-L3 Price and proposal

Website design and development starts **from £2,000**. A quote is calculated from requirements, the complexity of journeys and systems, and the deliverables written into the proposal. Never estimate a final price yourself. If a prospect pushes for a number, say the published starting price, explain the boundary and offer a proper quote or the Business Growth Audit.

### C02-L4 Timelines

**Source:** faq:timeline. Timing is confirmed after discovery because content readiness, integrations, review cycles and technical risk change the schedule more than page count. The proposal records the range and its assumptions. **Do not give a timeline.**

### C02-L5 Ownership and editing

**Sources:** faq:website-ownership, faq:code-ownership, faq:self-editing.

Ownership of the bespoke deliverable is set out in the signed project documents and transfers once agreed fees are paid. Clients keep their own materials, trademarks and data. ScaleSmiths keeps its pre-existing tools and know-how, and open-source components stay under their own licences.

Self-editing is a scoping decision: an editable content layer is worth building when content changes often. Ask the client what they expect to change, and how often.

### C02-L6 Technology and WordPress

**Source:** faq:wordpress (*owner review flagged*). Published work is custom-built rather than WordPress themes. If a client runs WordPress, ScaleSmiths looks at what it does well before recommending whether a rebuild is justified. Never criticise a client's current platform or supplier.

### C02-L7 Good-fit signals

An established business with clear services; a site that no longer reflects the business; enquiries that matter commercially; evidence worth protecting; an owner willing to engage with discovery. Weaker fit: wants the cheapest possible page, wants guaranteed rankings, or cannot give time to review.

### C02-L8 When it is not a standard website

Route these to ScaleSmiths before saying anything about price: e-commerce (faq:ecommerce-builds: custom commerce only where its value justifies owning it), booking or quote workflows, customer portals, payments, integrations, migrations and anything with user accounts. Request **technical scoping**.

---

## C03 SEO and Digital Growth

### C03-L1 What SEO is

**Source:** faq:what-is-seo. SEO makes a website findable, understandable and worth choosing in search results. It has three parts: technical foundations that let search engines crawl and index pages, content that answers what people actually search for, and an on-page experience that turns a click into an enquiry. It is ongoing work, not a setting.

### C03-L2 Local SEO

**Source:** faq:what-is-local-seo. Local SEO targets people looking for a provider in a place. It depends on clear service and area descriptions, consistent business details across the web, a Google Business Profile that supports the site, and visible local proof.

### C03-L3 Technical SEO

**Source:** faq:technical-seo. Crawlability and robots rules, canonical URLs, sitemaps, redirects, structured data, heading hierarchy, mobile rendering, Core Web Vitals and HTTPS. It rarely wins attention on its own, but content cannot perform if the technical layer works against it.

### C03-L4 Timescales and guarantees

**Sources:** faq:seo-timeline, faq:ranking-guarantees.

Technical fixes can change indexation quickly. Content and authority work is measured over months. **No one can guarantee first place on Google**, because rankings depend on Google's systems, competitors and the searcher.

**Say it like this:** "No honest agency can promise a position. What ScaleSmiths commits to is the work: technical health, content that matches real searches, credible proof, and measuring progress against a recorded baseline."

### C03-L5 Build versus ongoing

Search foundations are part of every build. Ongoing SEO (content, authority, measurement and iteration) is separate, scoped as a project or through a Growth Partnership.

### C03-L6 SEO and paid search

**Source:** faq:seo-and-google-ads. Ads buy visibility immediately and stop when the budget does; SEO compounds slowly. The right mix depends on urgency, margin and competition. ScaleSmiths will say when paid search is the more honest answer.

### C03-L7 What AI search and AEO mean

**Sources:** service listing "SEO/AEO landing pages" (`web/src/lib/service-pages.ts`), `web/src/lib/agent-discovery.ts`. *[FOUNDER DECISION `AP-CNT-06`: no published FAQ answer covers AI search yet. This lesson is new wording.]*

People increasingly ask AI assistants and AI-generated search summaries for recommendations. Answer engine optimisation (AEO) means making a site's content easy for those systems to understand and cite: pages that answer a buyer's real question directly, consistent facts, structured data and FAQ content, and clear service and location pages. ScaleSmiths builds pages this way and describes its own capabilities accurately in machine-readable form.

What you must not say: that ScaleSmiths can get a business "into ChatGPT", guarantee being cited, or control what any AI system says. Those systems are run by third parties and change often.

**Say it like this:** "Clear, well-structured answers help both search engines and AI assistants understand a business. Nobody can guarantee what an AI tool will say, but we can make sure your site gives it accurate, useful answers to work from."

### C03-L8 Diagnosing "not on Google"

**Source:** faq:not-on-google. The usual causes, in order: pages not indexed (robots rules, a noindex tag or a staging setting left on); indexed but not matching what people search for; or competing for terms far above the site's authority. Search Console usually separates these quickly, which is why the Business Growth Audit starts there.

---

## C04 Growth Partnerships

### C04-L1 What a Growth Partnership is

**Sources:** `web/src/app/digital-growth-partnership/page.tsx`, faq:support-included.

An ongoing partnership that can cover SEO, conversion, content, analytics, automation and technical support, whether or not ScaleSmiths built the current site. The proposal defines priorities, working cadence, responsibilities and commercial terms.

### C04-L2 What it is not

It is not an unlimited marketing package, not just maintenance, and not a promise of results. Maintenance protects dependable operation; SEO, content, design changes and integrations are improvement work and are scoped as such.

### C04-L3 Price and term

The published price is **from £350 per month**. The proposal sets the final scope and price. *[PROPOSED POLICY: the draft programme models a twelve-month minimum term (`standard-v2`, disabled). Whether, and how, a minimum term is presented to clients is founder decision `AP-COM-03`. Until then, do not mention a term.]*

### C04-L4 Roadmap and priorities

**Source:** faq:request-priority. Work follows an agreed roadmap and a prioritised backlog, not a first-come queue. Incidents affecting a live service come first. Clients raise and track requests in the ScaleSmiths client portal.

### C04-L5 Hosting, email and monitoring

**Sources:** faq:hosting-included, faq:monitoring. Hosting can be part of a Growth Partnership or a separate managed service; the order states what is covered. Monitoring is scoped to the actual stack. Business email is separate unless combined in writing.

### C04-L6 After a build

**Source:** faq:support. Launch is a measurement point, not the end. The production site is verified, measurement connected and ownership of accounts agreed. A Growth Partnership can then continue the work.

### C04-L7 Existing websites

**Source:** faq:manage-external-site. ScaleSmiths can often manage a site it did not build, after reviewing its code, hosting, access and update path. That review may identify prerequisite repairs, or show the platform needs its original specialist. It will not take on an unknown system blind.

---

## C05 Website Migration

### C05-L1 Types of migration

A platform rebuild (for example WordPress or Shopify to custom), a hosting move, a domain change, or a content-management change. Each has different risks. Many projects combine several.

### C05-L2 WordPress and Shopify moves

**Sources:** faq:website-migration, faq:rebuilds. ScaleSmiths reviews current code, licences, data, deployment and connected services first, then recommends a rebuild, a focused repair or a migration, whichever the evidence supports. Pinkys Prints is a published example: a Shopify store rebuilt as a custom platform and moved onto self-hosted infrastructure.

### C05-L3 Redirects and search risk

**Source:** faq:seo-rebuild (*owner review flagged*). Any rebuild carries some search risk and nobody can honestly guarantee rankings. Risk is reduced by mapping old URLs to new ones with redirects, carrying over content that performs, preserving metadata and structured data, and checking indexing after launch.

### C05-L4 What to collect

Who controls the domain and registrar; current hosting; access to the site's admin; Google Search Console and analytics access (if any); a list of integrations (forms, booking, payments, email marketing); any plugin or theme licences; and the business's deadline (for example a hosting contract ending).

### C05-L5 Red flags

Nobody knows who controls the domain; the domain is close to expiry; the previous supplier holds all access; unlicensed or abandoned plugins; data held only in the old platform; a hard deadline within weeks. None of these is a reason to walk away, but every one is a reason to escalate early.

### C05-L6 Escalation

Every migration goes to **technical scoping** before any price or timeline is discussed. Share what you collected in C05-L4.

---

## C06 Bespoke Software and Automation

### C06-L1 Custom versus off the shelf

**Source:** faq:custom-software. Custom software is justified when the workflow genuinely differentiates the business, when existing tools create material friction, or when integration and data-ownership needs cannot be met by configuration. If a proven product already fits, buying and integrating it is usually better, and ScaleSmiths will say so.

### C06-L2 What we have built

**Sources:** faq:crm (*owner review flagged*), faq:customer-portals, faq:stripe, faq:integrations, faq:internal-admin-systems.

Published examples, described as the FAQ library describes them:

- a private PostgreSQL-backed CRM for Confirm-A-Kill (enquiries, customers, properties, quotations, appointments, jobs, visits);
- a quote management admin behind the CSDS website;
- Stripe subscription billing for The Business Circle; plans, seats and credits for Prymal;
- booking integration and review aggregation for Glow Tanning;
- product and catalogue administration for Pinkys Prints;
- member and admin applications for VeteranFinder;
- ScaleSmiths' own client portal, with tenant isolation enforced on the server.

Describe what was built. Do not quote outcomes, figures or client opinions unless an approved resource contains them (`AP-PROOF-01`).

### C06-L3 Automating a workflow

**Source:** faq:process-automation. Start with one bounded workflow whose owner, inputs, exceptions and useful outcome can be defined. Good automation removes repeated handling while keeping the decisions people still need to make; high-consequence steps keep a human review point and a record.

### C06-L4 Spreadsheets and manual processes

**Source:** faq:replace-spreadsheets. Replace gradually, beginning with the highest-friction workflow. Rebuilding everything at once is the common failure.

### C06-L5 AI, honestly

Deterministic rules and integrations are often safer and cheaper than a language model. AI is used where interpretation is genuinely required. Do not sell "AI" as a feature in itself.

### C06-L6 Phases and scoping

**Sources:** faq:phases, faq:software-scaling, `engagement-models.ts`. Custom work is scoped after discovery and never priced against a website starting price. The first release has a defined boundary; later phases extend a system that is understood.

### C06-L7 Bespoke discovery requests

Request a **bespoke discovery** meeting when the client describes a workflow, system or integration rather than a website. Include: the workflow in the client's words, the people involved, current tools, rough volumes, what goes wrong today, and any deadline. *[PROPOSED POLICY: bespoke commission eligibility and existing-customer attribution are open founder decisions.]*

# Initial lesson content: courses 7 to 13

**Status: DRAFT. Not approved, not published, not for use with partners or clients.** Courses C07, C11 and C12 are also `BLOCKED` on founder, legal and accounting decisions; see [CURRICULUM.md](CURRICULUM.md). Conventions are as in [LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md](LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md).

---

## C07 Finding Prospects (BLOCKED: marketing process)

### C07-L1 Good-fit businesses

Look for established businesses with a clear offer and customers who search before they buy: trades, professional services, health and clinics, local retail, specialist manufacturers. Signals: an outdated or slow site, weak mobile experience, no clear route to enquire, services missing from the site, or an owner who talks about growth. Weaker fit: no budget at all, wants a template, or wants a guarantee.

### C07-L2 Warm introductions

Your own professional network is the best starting point. Introduce people who would genuinely benefit, ask before passing on anyone's details, and be open that you are an independent partner of ScaleSmiths.

### C07-L3 Registering a prospect

Register a prospect in the Partner Portal before detailed conversations. Registration is a preliminary record: duplicates and existing clients are checked, and lead protection applies to ordinary registrations. *[FOUNDER DECISION `AP-COM-06`: the lead protection term, expiry and dispute process are not approved. Do not tell a partner or prospect how long protection lasts.]*

### C07-L4 Researched prospects

*[PROPOSED POLICY]* ScaleSmiths may allocate researched businesses, subject to availability, screening and market approval. No fixed number is guaranteed and nothing is contacted by ScaleSmiths on your behalf. Treat each allocated business as **not assessed for outreach** until the approved process says otherwise.

### C07-L5 Contact rules

*[BLOCKED: approved marketing process, `AP-LEG-03`]* Direct marketing is regulated. For UK business-to-business marketing calls, the ICO directs organisations to check the TPS and CTPS registers and their own do-not-call lists, and electronic marketing rules vary by channel and subscriber type ([ICO guidance](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/)). Until ScaleSmiths approves a process, **do not make unsolicited calls or send unsolicited marketing emails on ScaleSmiths' behalf.**

### C07-L6 Suppression and objections

If someone asks not to be contacted, stop, record it in the portal and tell ScaleSmiths. Never argue with an opt-out or try another channel.

### C07-L7 Sectors and exclusivity

Some clients may have sector exclusivity. If the portal shows "commercial checks in progress", that is all you will be told. The details are confidential and decided by founders. Do not guess or ask the prospect about competitors.

---

## C08 Discovery Meetings

### C08-L1 Preparing

Spend fifteen minutes before the meeting: read their website on a phone, search for their main service and town, note whether they appear, check whether they have a Google Business Profile, and read any reviews. Use [R09 Meeting preparation checklist](resources/R09-meeting-preparation-checklist.md). Note questions, not conclusions.

### C08-L2 Setting the agenda

Open with purpose and time: "I'd like to understand how the business wins customers today and where the website helps or gets in the way. Then, if it makes sense, I'll explain how ScaleSmiths could help and what the next step would be." Confirm how long they have.

### C08-L3 The core questions

Use [R07 Discovery questionnaire](resources/R07-discovery-questionnaire.md). The essentials:

1. What do you sell, and which services matter most commercially?
2. Who are your best customers and how do they find you?
3. What does your current website do well? What frustrates you?
4. What evidence do you have: enquiries, calls, analytics, Search Console?
5. What systems do you use (booking, CRM, email, payments)?
6. Who controls the domain, hosting and website accounts?
7. What would a good result look like in a year?
8. Is there a deadline or trigger?
9. Have you set aside a budget range?

### C08-L4 Listening for fit

- "We look dated / we don't get enquiries from the site" → website project.
- "We have a decent site but nobody finds it" → Business Growth Audit or Growth Partnership.
- "We're not sure what's wrong" → Business Growth Audit.
- "We run everything on spreadsheets / our booking is a mess" → bespoke discovery.
- "Our emails go to spam / we use a Gmail address" → Managed Business Email.

### C08-L5 What not to say

No prices beyond the four published starting prices. No timelines. No rankings, traffic or revenue predictions. No commitments about what is included. No criticism of their current supplier. No mention of your commission.

### C08-L6 Writing up

Write notes the same day in the questionnaire format: facts they told you, your observations (clearly marked as yours), open questions and the agreed next step.

### C08-L7 Next steps

Offer one clear next step: a quote request, the Business Growth Audit (£395), a joint sales meeting, or technical scoping. Confirm it in writing using [R13 Follow-up templates](resources/R13-follow-up-templates.md).

---

## C09 Presenting ScaleSmiths

### C09-L1 Problem first

Open by playing back what you heard: "You said most new customers come from referrals, and the site doesn't explain your commercial services." Then connect each part of your presentation to one of those points.

### C09-L2 The ScaleSmiths approach

Four points, each from published wording: protect what already works; write the scope down; deliver in phases with a dependable first release; measure against agreed signals instead of invented targets.

### C09-L3 Using published work

You may describe what was built for published clients as the FAQ library and case studies describe it (see C06-L2), once founders approve partner use (`AP-PROOF-01`). Point people to the case studies on the ScaleSmiths website instead of retelling them.

### C09-L4 Proof you must not use

Testimonials or quotes not shown on the site; outcome figures that are not in an approved resource; client names that are not published; "we've helped hundreds of businesses"-style claims; screenshots of private systems.

### C09-L5 Presenting price

State the relevant published starting price and the boundary. Suggest the Business Growth Audit where the need is unclear: it is a one-time review and prioritised roadmap, and where the published terms apply the full fee is credited against an eligible subsequent ScaleSmiths build.

### C09-L6 A respectful close

"Would it help if I arranged a proper quote?" is enough. Agree a date to follow up. Never use false urgency ("this price ends Friday").

---

## C10 Objection Handling

The full set of responses, with approval status for each, is in [R08 Objection-handling playbook](resources/R08-objection-handling-playbook.md).

### C10-L1 The pattern

1. **Acknowledge** the concern without arguing.
2. **Clarify** what is behind it with a question.
3. **Answer** with approved wording.
4. **Confirm** whether that helps, and agree the next step.

### C10-L2 When to stop

Stop if the business is not a good fit, if the person is under pressure or vulnerable, or if the objection needs ScaleSmiths (contract terms, technical risk, a complaint about a previous supplier, a legal question). Saying "that's a question for ScaleSmiths; I'll get you a proper answer" is a good outcome.

### C10-L3 "It is too expensive"

Clarify: compared with what, and for what scope? Explain that a starting price is an entry point for an agreed scope, that proposals list what is included, that work can be phased, and that the Business Growth Audit is a lower-cost first step. **Never offer a discount.** Discount allowances are disabled and only founders can reserve one *[PROPOSED POLICY]*.

### C10-L4 "We already have a website or an agency"

Respect the existing relationship. ScaleSmiths starts by reviewing what currently works. An audit can serve as an independent second opinion, and its findings are useful whoever implements them.

### C10-L5 "Can you guarantee results?"

No. Use the approved line from C03-L4. Explain that commitments are to the work and to measuring against a baseline.

### C10-L6 "We use WordPress, Wix or Shopify"

ScaleSmiths is not anti-platform. It looks at what the current platform is doing well before recommending whether a rebuild is justified, and where an established platform fits, configuring it may be the better decision.

### C10-L7 "We need to think about it"

Agree, summarise what you discussed, offer to send a short written summary, and agree when to follow up.

### C10-L8 Using the objection workspace

Search for the objection in the client's words, read the partner guidance, then copy only the **client-facing** line. Practise responses aloud. Report new objections to ScaleSmiths so an approved answer can be written.

---

## C11 Commercial Policies (BLOCKED: agreement and terms)

> Every partner-term figure in this course is **PROPOSED POLICY**: an illustration of the proposed programme, not an approved agreement. Plans are disabled by default. No reward is payable. This course must not be published until the decisions listed in [CURRICULUM.md](CURRICULUM.md) are recorded.

### C11-L1 Published starting prices

Website from £2,000; Growth Partnership from £350 per month; Business Growth Audit £395; business email from £15 per month. GBP, and always with the starting-price boundary.

### C11-L2 Proposals and payment terms

**Source:** faq:deposit. Payment terms, including any staged or upfront payment, are set in each proposal and signed order. There is no blanket published deposit policy. Never describe a payment schedule to a client.

### C11-L3 How commission is proposed to work

*[PROPOSED POLICY]* Source: `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts`, [COMMISSION-RULES.md](../COMMISSION-RULES.md).

- Commission is proposed at **30% of eligible payments actually collected**, VAT-exclusive, under the final partner agreement.
- For a standard website plan it applies to the build fee and the **first** Growth Partnership payment only. Later monthly payments earn no acquisition commission.
- Only payments a ScaleSmiths founder has verified as collected count. A pending contract value is never earned.
- Commission is calculated once on the cumulative amount, so splitting payments cannot change the total.
- Refunds do not reduce commission automatically; they are held for founder review (refund treatment is undecided).

### C11-L4 Worked examples

*[PROPOSED POLICY, accountant review required]*

| Scenario | Client payments (ex VAT) | Proposed commission |
|---|---|---|
| Standard website + first Growth Partnership payment | £2,000 + £350 | £600 + £105 = **£705** |
| Discounted build at £1,500 (founder-approved only) | £1,500 + £350 | £450 + £105 = **£555** |
| Growth Partnership only | first £350 | **£105** |
| Bespoke project, £10,000 eligible collected | £10,000 | **£3,000** (30% unless a different approved rate) |

Payment order (deposit then balance, or equal instalments) does not change the total. Commission becomes due only as payments are collected and verified.

### C11-L5 What is not decided

Withdrawal frequency, minimum and invoicing; partner VAT treatment; refund and clawback treatment; achievement rewards (planned, not payable); the partner referral reward (planned, not payable); market approval (no market, including the UK, is approved yet); discount allowances (none approved).

### C11-L6 What you may and may not agree

You may: share the published starting prices, explain the starting-price boundary, and arrange a quote. You may not: agree a price, discount, payment schedule, timeline, scope or contract term, or describe your commission to a client.

### C11-L7 Markets

All prices are GBP. No international pricing, tax treatment or currency conversion exists. A customer's market must be approved by founders before a contract can be accepted.

---

## C12 Professional Conduct (BLOCKED: agreement and solicitor review)

### C12-L1 Independent, not employed

*[PROPOSED POLICY, employment solicitor review `AP-GOV-02`]* The partnership is an independent, commission-only arrangement. There is no salary, guaranteed income, compulsory working hours or sales target. You choose whether to use the Academy. Any future employed role would be a separate offer with its own agreement, and nothing about that is guaranteed.

### C12-L2 How to describe yourself

Use the approved title once decided (`AP-GOV-05`; the draft programme uses "Independent Business Partner"). Say "I'm an independent partner of ScaleSmiths", not "I work for ScaleSmiths". Never imply that you are an employee, director, owner or shareholder.

### C12-L3 Truthful representation

Use approved content only. No guarantees, invented proof, unapproved prices or claims about features that are planned or in development. If you are unsure, say you will check.

### C12-L4 Pressure and vulnerability

No pressure selling, false urgency or repeated contact after a "no". Take extra care if someone seems confused, distressed or not in a position to make a business decision; stop and tell ScaleSmiths.

### C12-L5 Personal data

*[Privacy adviser review `AP-PRIV-01`]* Collect only what is needed to register and discuss an opportunity. Record it in the Partner Portal, not in personal spreadsheets or messaging apps. Never ask a client for passwords; ScaleSmiths uses delegated or scoped access and never asks for registrar passwords through a public form (faq:dns).

### C12-L6 Confidentiality

Commission terms, other partners, exclusivity, internal resources marked "Partner only" and anything a founder shares in confidence stay private.

### C12-L7 Complaints and mistakes

If a client complains, or you realise you said something wrong, tell ScaleSmiths the same day through an **escalation** meeting request. Correcting a mistake early is always better than covering it.

---

## C13 Advanced and Enterprise Opportunities

### C13-L1 Established business transformation

**Source:** `engagement-models.ts`. Multi-site and established organisations that have outgrown a brochure site: customer journeys, integrations and operational efficiency across a digital estate.

### C13-L2 Custom platforms and enterprise

Bespoke architecture, workflows, security, migrations and support for complex platforms. See the `/enterprise` and `/enterprise-websites` pages for the published positioning.

### C13-L3 Scoped after discovery

Complex work is never sold against a starting price. Do not suggest a range. ScaleSmiths runs discovery and writes the scope.

Spend fifteen minutes before the meeting: read their website on a phone, search for their main service and town, note whether they appear, check whether they have a Google Business Profile, and read any reviews. Use [R09 Meeting preparation checklist](resources/R09-meeting-preparation-checklist.md). Note questions, not conclusions.

Open with purpose and time: "I'd like to understand how the business wins customers today and where the website helps or gets in the way. Then, if it makes sense, I'll explain how ScaleSmiths could help and what the next step would be." Confirm how long they have.

2. Who are your best customers and how do they find you?

- "We run everything on spreadsheets / our booking is a mess" → bespoke discovery.

### C08-L5 What not to say

No prices beyond the four published starting prices. No timelines. No rankings, traffic or revenue predictions. No commitments about what is included. No criticism of their current supplier. No mention of your commission.

Write notes the same day in the questionnaire format: facts they told you, your observations (clearly marked as yours), open questions and the agreed next step.

Offer one clear next step: a quote request, the Business Growth Audit (£395), a joint sales meeting, or technical scoping. Confirm it in writing using [R13 Follow-up templates](resources/R13-follow-up-templates.md).

## C07 Finding Prospects (BLOCKED: marketing process)

### C07-L1 Good-fit businesses

Look for established businesses with a clear offer and customers who search before they buy: trades, professional services, health and clinics, local retail, specialist manufacturers. Signals: an outdated or slow site, weak mobile experience, no clear route to enquire, services missing from the site, or an owner who talks about growth. Weaker fit: no budget at all, wants a template, or wants a guarantee.

### C07-L2 Warm introductions

Your own professional network is the best starting point. Introduce people who would genuinely benefit, ask before passing on anyone's details, and be open that you are an independent partner of ScaleSmiths.

### C07-L3 Registering a prospect

Register a prospect in the Partner Portal before detailed conversations. Registration is a preliminary record: duplicates and existing clients are checked, and lead protection applies to ordinary registrations. *[FOUNDER DECISION `AP-COM-06`: the lead protection term, expiry and dispute process are not approved. Do not tell a partner or prospect how long protection lasts.]*

### C07-L4 Researched prospects

*[PROPOSED POLICY]* ScaleSmiths may allocate researched businesses, subject to availability, screening and market approval. No fixed number is guaranteed and nothing is contacted by ScaleSmiths on your behalf. Treat each allocated business as **not assessed for outreach** until the approved process says otherwise.

### C07-L5 Contact rules

*[BLOCKED: approved marketing process, `AP-LEG-03`]* Direct marketing is regulated. For UK business-to-business marketing calls, the ICO directs organisations to check the TPS and CTPS registers and their own do-not-call lists, and electronic marketing rules vary by channel and subscriber type ([ICO guidance](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/)). Until ScaleSmiths approves a process, **do not make unsolicited calls or send unsolicited marketing emails on ScaleSmiths' behalf.**

### C07-L6 Suppression and objections

If someone asks not to be contacted, stop, record it in the portal and tell ScaleSmiths. Never argue with an opt-out or try another channel.

### C07-L7 Sectors and exclusivity

Some clients may have sector exclusivity. If the portal shows "commercial checks in progress", that is all you will be told. The details are confidential and decided by founders. Do not guess or ask the prospect about competitors.

---

## C08 Discovery Meetings

### C08-L1 Preparing

Spend fifteen minutes before the meeting: read their website on a phone, search for their main service and town, note whether they appear, check whether they have a Google Business Profile, and read any reviews. Use [R09 Meeting preparation checklist](resources/R09-meeting-preparation-checklist.md). Note questions, not conclusions.

### C08-L2 Setting the agenda

Open with purpose and time: "I'd like to understand how the business wins customers today and where the website helps or gets in the way. Then, if it makes sense, I'll explain how ScaleSmiths could help and what the next step would be." Confirm how long they have.

### C08-L3 The core questions

Use [R07 Discovery questionnaire](resources/R07-discovery-questionnaire.md). The essentials:

1. What do you sell, and which services matter most commercially?
2. Who are your best customers and how do they find you?
3. What does your current website do well? What frustrates you?
4. What evidence do you have: enquiries, calls, analytics, Search Console?
5. What systems do you use (booking, CRM, email, payments)?
6. Who controls the domain, hosting and website accounts?
7. What would a good result look like in a year?
8. Is there a deadline or trigger?
9. Have you set aside a budget range?

### C08-L4 Listening for fit

- "We look dated / we don't get enquiries from the site" → website project.
- "We have a decent site but nobody finds it" → Business Growth Audit or Growth Partnership.
- "We're not sure what's wrong" → Business Growth Audit.
- "We run everything on spreadsheets / our booking is a mess" → bespoke discovery.
- "Our emails go to spam / we use a Gmail address" → Managed Business Email.

### C08-L5 What not to say

No prices beyond the four published starting prices. No timelines. No rankings, traffic or revenue predictions. No commitments about what is included. No criticism of their current supplier. No mention of your commission.

### C08-L6 Writing up

Write notes the same day in the questionnaire format: facts they told you, your observations (clearly marked as yours), open questions and the agreed next step.

### C08-L7 Next steps

Offer one clear next step: a quote request, the Business Growth Audit (£395), a joint sales meeting, or technical scoping. Confirm it in writing using [R13 Follow-up templates](resources/R13-follow-up-templates.md).

---

## C09 Presenting ScaleSmiths

### C09-L1 Problem first

Open by playing back what you heard: "You said most new customers come from referrals, and the site doesn't explain your commercial services." Then connect each part of your presentation to one of those points.

### C09-L2 The ScaleSmiths approach

Four points, each from published wording: protect what already works; write the scope down; deliver in phases with a dependable first release; measure against agreed signals instead of invented targets.

### C09-L3 Using published work

You may describe what was built for published clients as the FAQ library and case studies describe it (see C06-L2), once founders approve partner use (`AP-PROOF-01`). Point people to the case studies on the ScaleSmiths website instead of retelling them.

### C09-L4 Proof you must not use

Testimonials or quotes not shown on the site; outcome figures that are not in an approved resource; client names that are not published; "we've helped hundreds of businesses"-style claims; screenshots of private systems.

### C09-L5 Presenting price

State the relevant published starting price and the boundary. Suggest the Business Growth Audit where the need is unclear: it is a one-time review and prioritised roadmap, and where the published terms apply the full fee is credited against an eligible subsequent ScaleSmiths build.

### C09-L6 A respectful close

"Would it help if I arranged a proper quote?" is enough. Agree a date to follow up. Never use false urgency ("this price ends Friday").

---

## C10 Objection Handling

The full set of responses, with approval status for each, is in [R08 Objection-handling playbook](resources/R08-objection-handling-playbook.md).

### C10-L1 The pattern

1. **Acknowledge** the concern without arguing.
2. **Clarify** what is behind it with a question.
3. **Answer** with approved wording.
4. **Confirm** whether that helps, and agree the next step.

### C10-L2 When to stop

Stop if the business is not a good fit, if the person is under pressure or vulnerable, or if the objection needs ScaleSmiths (contract terms, technical risk, a complaint about a previous supplier, a legal question). Saying "that's a question for ScaleSmiths; I'll get you a proper answer" is a good outcome.

### C10-L3 "It is too expensive"

Clarify: compared with what, and for what scope? Explain that a starting price is an entry point for an agreed scope, that proposals list what is included, that work can be phased, and that the Business Growth Audit is a lower-cost first step. **Never offer a discount.** Discount allowances are disabled and only founders can reserve one *[PROPOSED POLICY]*.

Respect the existing relationship. ScaleSmiths starts by reviewing what currently works. An audit can serve as an independent second opinion, and its findings are useful whoever implements them.

ScaleSmiths is not anti-platform. It looks at what the current platform is doing well before recommending whether a rebuild is justified, and where an established platform fits, configuring it may be the better decision.

Agree, summarise what you discussed, offer to send a short written summary, and agree when to follow up.

Search for the objection in the client's words, read the partner guidance, then copy only the **client-facing** line. Practise responses aloud. Report new objections to ScaleSmiths so an approved answer can be written.

This handbook explains how the ScaleSmiths partnership works day to day. It is a practical guide, not a contract.

## 2. Your relationship with ScaleSmiths

*[PROPOSED POLICY, solicitor review]* You are an independent partner, not an employee. There is no salary, guaranteed income, compulsory working hours or sales target. You decide whether, when and how you work, and whether to use the Partner Academy. Commission is gross, before your own expenses and tax.

## 3. What you do and what ScaleSmiths does

| You | ScaleSmiths |
|---|---|
| Identify and introduce suitable businesses | Reviews every opportunity |
| Hold early, honest conversations | Scopes, prices and writes proposals |
| Register prospects in the portal | Contracts with and invoices the client |
| Support the relationship | Delivers and supports the work |
| Pass on questions | Answers technical, commercial and legal questions |

Use only approved, published content. Each item shows its version, approval date and review date, and whether it is **client-facing** or **partner only**. If an answer is not in the portal, ask; do not improvise.

Register before detailed conversations. Duplicates and existing clients are checked. *[FOUNDER DECISION `AP-COM-06`: lead protection start, expiry, reassignment and disputes.]*

*[BLOCKED `AP-LEG-03`: approved marketing process.]* Until the process is approved, work through your own network and introductions, and do not make unsolicited calls or send unsolicited marketing emails on ScaleSmiths' behalf.

Request a meeting in the portal: joint sales, technical scoping, bespoke discovery, commercial assistance, proposal review, training or escalation. See [R10 Technical escalation guide](R10-technical-escalation-guide.md).

## 9. Commission

See [R12 Commission and payment reference](R12-commission-and-payment-reference.md). Everything there is proposed until the agreement and terms are approved.

## 10. Conduct

Be truthful, never pressure anyone, protect personal data, keep confidential information private, and tell ScaleSmiths quickly about complaints or mistakes. The Professional Conduct course (C12) expands on this.

## 11. Personal data

*[Privacy adviser review `AP-PRIV-01`]* Collect only what you need; store it in the portal; never ask clients for passwords; respect every request not to be contacted.

## 12. Ending the partnership

*[FOUNDER DECISION: per the agreement, including what happens to registered prospects and commission on payments collected afterwards.]*
